title: HVO-ARBiH Fighting Erupts at Gornji Vakuf
narrative: Heavy fighting breaks out between HVO and ARBiH forces in Gornji Vakuf as the HVO attempts to establish control over the town in line with the proposed Vance-Owen provincial boundaries. The clashes — involving tanks, artillery, and infantry — mark a significant escalation beyond the sporadic incidents of late 1992.
historical_source: ICTY Prlic et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment Vol. 2 §§221-310 and Vol. 4 §§44-67; Prlic Appeals Judgment §§601-650; Blaskic IT-95-14-T §§161-220; Kordic IT-95-14/2-T §§560-650; Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II pp. 448, 452; docs/40_reports/1993_EVENT_RESEARCH.md.
source_note: BB Vol. II frames Gornji Vakuf as an early 1993 HVO-ARBiH escalation around the Vance-Owen provincial map; the local response choice is a command-posture abstraction. Per Sensitive History Gate §1.5 #11 the escalate posture is operational-tempo only — specific atrocities (Dusa, Bistrica, Zdrimci) emerge from Ring 1 combat / paramilitary / displacement engines and Ring 2 essays, not from this row's effects.
staff_assessment: Escalating reinforces the local HVO position but deepens the command split with ARBiH; a ceasefire contains the front at the cost of initiative and morale.
trigger_evidence: Alliance cohesion has fallen below the cooperation threshold.
The Vance-Owen provincial map has made central Bosnia command boundaries contested.
HVO and ARBiH units are already fighting around Gornji Vakuf.

effects.text: HVO and ARBiH forces fight a pitched battle at Gornji Vakuf. The Vance-Owen provincial map becomes a pretext for Croat territorial grabs.

response_options.label: Respond with force
response_options.description: Send reinforcements to Gornji Vakuf. Escalates the confrontation significantly.

response_options.label: Seek a local ceasefire
response_options.description: Attempt to contain the fighting. De-escalates but does not resolve underlying tensions.

RBiH.headline: HVO reinforces Gornji Vakuf fight
RBiH.body: Herceg-Bosna sends reinforcements into the Gornji Vakuf clashes. Sarajevo staff see a significant escalation in the HVO-ARBiH confrontation and a sharper break in local cooperation.

RS.headline: HVO and ARBiH fighting intensifies
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna answers the Gornji Vakuf clashes with force. Pale analysts see the Vance-Owen provincial map becoming a boundary dispute for deeper Croat-Bosniak fighting.

RBiH.headline: HVO seeks a local Gornji Vakuf ceasefire
RBiH.body: Herceg-Bosna tries to contain the fighting around Gornji Vakuf. Sarajevo sees de-escalation on the local front, though the underlying territorial dispute remains unresolved.

RS.headline: Gornji Vakuf fighting is contained for now
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna moves toward a local ceasefire rather than a wider escalation. Pale reads the alliance strain as real, but not yet a full rupture.

title: Western Powers Press Sarajevo: Engage with Vance-Owen
narrative: Western capitals and mediators increase pressure on Sarajevo to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. The diplomatic sequence signals that refusal would risk isolating the government internationally.
historical_source: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. I pp.6-8; UN S/25479; UNSCR 820.
source_note: The pressure is inferred from the Vance-Owen diplomatic sequence and Western/UN escalation around April 1993; this row avoids attributing an unsourced direct warning to any single mediator.
staff_assessment: Acknowledging the pressure preserves international confidence but costs leverage and internal cohesion; resisting protects Sarajevo's position while risking diplomatic isolation.
trigger_evidence: The Vance-Owen process is entering its final acceptance window.
UN S/25479 and UNSCR 820 show international pressure escalating around the plan.
Sarajevo's continued engagement is becoming central to preserving Western diplomatic support.

effect.text: Western capitals press Sarajevo to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan or risk international isolation.

response_options.label: Acknowledge the message
response_options.description: Engage the Vance-Owen process to preserve Western confidence, while accepting some loss of leverage and domestic cohesion.

response_options.label: Maintain our position
response_options.description: Hold Sarajevo's negotiating line despite mediator and Western pressure, preserving claims but risking international confidence.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo engages Vance-Owen pressure
HRHB.body: RBiH acknowledges Western pressure to engage seriously with the Vance-Owen Peace Plan. HVO staff see a more cooperative diplomatic posture, even as Sarajevo absorbs internal strain.

RS.headline: Sarajevo answers Western pressure
RS.body: RBiH signals that it will engage with the Vance-Owen process to preserve international support. Pale sees Sarajevo trading some leverage for patron confidence.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo holds its Vance-Owen line
HRHB.body: RBiH maintains its position despite mounting mediator and Western pressure. HVO staff see Sarajevo preserving negotiating leverage while risking patron confidence.

RS.headline: Sarajevo resists mediator pressure
RS.body: RBiH refuses to soften its Vance-Owen stance under Western pressure. Pale reads the move as a bid for leverage, with a visible cost to Sarajevo's international support.

title: Vance-Owen Peace Plan Presented
narrative: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan proposes dividing Bosnia into ten semi-autonomous provinces based on ethnic and geographic criteria. The Bosnian Croat leadership endorses it, and RBiH reluctantly signs and accepts under pressure, but the Bosnian Serb assembly in Pale rejects it, dooming the most comprehensive peace effort to date.
historical_source: UN S/25479 (8 April 1993, Co-Chairmen's letter transmitting the agreed Vance-Owen Peace Plan); UN S/25221 (29 January 1993) and UN S/25403 (12 March 1993) earlier transmissions; UNSCR 820 (17 April 1993) and UNSCR 824 (6 May 1993); ICTY Karadžić Trial Judgement (IT-95-5/18-T, 24 March 2016) §§ on VOPP-rejection narrative; ICTY Prlić et al. Trial Judgement (IT-04-74, 29 May 2013) §§ on Croat-Bosniak VOPP-window relations; Bosnian Presidency records of the Athens signing of 25 March 1993; Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. I pp. 6-8.
source_note: The row represents Sarajevo's reluctant acceptance of the Vance-Owen framework under diplomatic pressure; it does not present the plan as a moral settlement or a delivered peace.
staff_assessment: Acceptance keeps Sarajevo aligned with Western diplomacy and shifts pressure toward Pale, but it means tolerating an externally drafted ten-province formula. Rejection preserves claims while damaging credibility.
trigger_evidence: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan has been formally presented.
Western and UN diplomacy is pressing the parties toward signatures.
Pale's assembly response remains the decisive obstacle after Sarajevo's pressured acceptance.

effect.text: The Vance-Owen Plan is presented. All parties must decide whether to accept a negotiated partition of Bosnia.

response_options.label: Accept the Vance-Owen Plan
response_options.description: Accepting improves international credibility and may bring relief, but legitimizes territorial losses.

response_options.label: Reject the Vance-Owen Plan
response_options.description: Rejection preserves territorial claims but damages standing with the international community.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen terms
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen Plan, improving international credibility while accepting a framework that legitimizes territorial losses. HVO leaders see Sarajevo moving into the same diplomatic channel.

RS.headline: Sarajevo accepts Vance-Owen
RS.body: RBiH accepts the Vance-Owen framework and gains international credibility. Pale sees Sarajevo accepting the partition formula while pressure shifts toward the Bosnian Serb assembly.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo rejects Vance-Owen
HRHB.body: RBiH rejects the Vance-Owen Plan to preserve territorial claims. HVO leaders see Sarajevo keeping freedom of action at the cost of international standing.

RS.headline: Sarajevo refuses Vance-Owen
RS.body: RBiH rejects the proposed ten-province settlement and preserves its territorial claims. Pale sees Sarajevo taking a morale gain while damaging its international standing.

title: Kravica Raid on Orthodox Christmas
narrative: ARBiH forces under Naser Oric launch a raid from the Srebrenica enclave on the Serb village of Kravica on Orthodox Christmas Day, killing between 30-35 VRS soldiers and 11-13 Serb civilians. The attack provides the VRS a pretext for intensifying its spring offensive against the eastern enclaves. Oric is later indicted by the ICTY for failing to prevent crimes in the enclave's defense.

effects.text: The Christmas raid on Kravica galvanizes VRS commanders. The Drina Corps begins preparations for an offensive to crush the eastern enclaves once and for all.

historical_source: ICTY Oric Indictment (IT-03-68). Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), paras. 17-18.

title: Deputy Prime Minister Turajlic Assassinated
narrative: VRS soldiers stop a UN convoy transporting Bosnian Deputy Prime Minister Hakija Turajlic from Sarajevo Airport. After a 90-minute standoff, a Serb soldier shoots Turajlic seven times through the open door of a French UNPROFOR APC, killing him in front of five peacekeepers. He is the highest-ranking Bosnian official killed in the war.

effects.text: The murder of Turajlic inside a UN vehicle exposes the fragility of UNPROFOR's protection and the VRS's contempt for international norms.

historical_source: ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T), para. 5778.

title: Croat-Bosniak War Erupts
narrative: Full-scale fighting erupts between the HVO and the ARBiH across central Bosnia and Herzegovina. Emboldened by the Vance-Owen provincial map and Croatian political pressure, HVO forces launch coordinated offensives to secure territories claimed for Herceg-Bosna. What began as sporadic clashes at Prozor and Gornji Vakuf escalates into systematic ethnic cleansing on both sides, opening a devastating second front for the Bosnian government.

effects.text: The Croat-Bosniak alliance collapses. HVO and ARBiH forces engage in open warfare across central Bosnia.

title: Ahmici Massacre
narrative: HVO forces, supported by the Jokers special police unit, launch a coordinated attack on the Bosniak village of Ahmici in the Lasva Valley. Over 100 civilians are killed, including women and children, and the village is systematically burned. The massacre becomes one of the most documented war crimes of the conflict and a defining atrocity of the Croat-Bosniak war.
source_note: Existing ICTY/UN and same-id essay sources ground the row's provenance and institutional context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effects.text: The Ahmici massacre shocks the international community. HVO credibility suffers a devastating blow.

title: US Special Envoy — American Engagement Begins
narrative: President Clinton names Ambassador Reginald Bartholomew as the first US special envoy to Bosnia negotiations, signaling increased American engagement with the conflict. In May, Secretary of State Warren Christopher proposes a 'lift and strike' policy — lifting the arms embargo and using air strikes against VRS positions — but Britain and France reject it. Despite this setback, American diplomatic involvement has begun in earnest.

effects.text: American diplomacy enters the Bosnian arena. The 'lift and strike' proposal fails in Europe, but Washington's trajectory toward intervention has begun.

historical_source: US State Department, 'Bosnia: Road to the Dayton Peace Agreement.'

title: VRS Cerska-Konjevic Polje Offensive
narrative: The VRS Drina Corps, supported by Yugoslav Army armor, launches Operation Cerska, overrunning Bosniak-held positions at Cerska and Konjevic Polje in eastern Bosnia. The offensive severs the land link between the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, reducing the Srebrenica pocket to 150 square kilometers and driving 50,000-60,000 refugees into the overcrowded town.

effects.text: Cerska and Konjevic Polje fall to the Drina Corps. Srebrenica is now completely isolated and bursting with refugees.

historical_source: ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), paras. 15-22. Mladic Trial Judgment (IT-09-92-T).

title: HVO Besieges East Mostar
narrative: HVO forces impose a complete blockade on the eastern bank of Mostar, cutting off the Bosniak population from food, water, and medical supplies. Systematic shelling targets the densely populated old town. An estimated 55,000 Bosniaks are trapped in increasingly desperate conditions as the HVO seeks to drive them from the city entirely.

effects.text: East Mostar is besieged. 55,000 Bosniaks are trapped as HVO forces impose a total blockade on the eastern bank.

title: UN Resolution 808 — International Tribunal Announced
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 808, deciding that an international tribunal shall be established for the prosecution of serious violations of international humanitarian law in the former Yugoslavia. The resolution signals growing judicial attention to wartime atrocities and serves as the direct precursor to the ICTY's formal establishment in May.

effects.text: Resolution 808 puts all commanders on notice: the international community is documenting crimes and building the architecture for prosecution.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 808 (1993), S/RES/808.

title: Central Bosnia Engulfed in Three-Way War
narrative: Central Bosnia becomes a patchwork of overlapping front lines as VRS, HVO, and ARBiH forces fight simultaneously. Towns like Travnik, Vitez, and Busovaca change hands or are divided street by street. The three-way nature of the conflict creates impossible tactical situations and widespread civilian suffering.
source_note: Existing event/essay/project sources ground the row's institutional and operational context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effect.text: Three-way fighting engulfs central Bosnia. The overlapping front lines create a humanitarian catastrophe.

title: Zagreb Restrains Boban: Hold Back During VOPP Window
narrative: Tuđman quietly orders Boban to restrain HVO offensive operations. The Vance-Owen provincial map is favorable to Croat Herzegovina — Zagreb needs HRHB to accept the plan, not derail it through military escalation. Boban signed the plan in Geneva on 2 January 1993 on Tudjman's direction, making HZ HB the first party to accept the ten-province framework.
historical_source: ICTY Prlić et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment (29 May 2013) Vol. 3 §§412-498 (HZ HB Presidency acceptance of VOPP and Province-3/8/10 provincial-map framework); Prlić Appeals Judgment (29 Nov 2017) §§612-650; Vance-Owen Plan agreement text UN S/25221 Annex VII (29 January 1993) and UN S/25403 Annex II (12 March 1993); Tuđman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3 §§460-485 (patron coordination directing Boban to sign); Prlić Vol. 2 §§220-260 (HV officer-secondment / fuel / ammunition support contingent on Zagreb axis); Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II diplomatic chronology January-May 1993.
source_note: The row represents Zagreb's restraint order on HVO offensive operations during the Vance-Owen acceptance window and the HZ HB Presidency's posture toward patron direction. Acknowledge-pressure is the documented historical choice (Boban signed at Geneva 2 January 1993 on Tudjman's direction). Resist-patron is a structurally plausible counterfactual — no HZ HB Presidency document opposes signature in the historical record, but the analogous patron-resistance precedent exists at R6 (RS Assembly rejection 5-6 May 1993).

effect.text: Zagreb quietly orders Boban to hold back HVO offensive operations during the Vance-Owen window.

title: General Morillon Enters Srebrenica
narrative: UNPROFOR Commander General Philippe Morillon reaches the besieged Srebrenica enclave after months of convoy blockades. Confronted by desperate civilians, he publicly declares 'You are now under the protection of the United Nations. I will never abandon you.' His personal guarantee raises hopes but lacks any enforcement mechanism.
source_note: ICTY Krstic and MSF sources ground the row's Srebrenica convoy and UNPROFOR context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effects.text: Morillon's dramatic declaration creates an obligation the UN cannot fulfill. The gap between his promise and UNPROFOR's means defines the enclave's tragic position.

historical_source: ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T), para. 20. MSF Speaking Out: Srebrenica 1993-2003.

title: Srebrenica Under Heavy Bombardment
narrative: The VRS intensifies its assault on the Srebrenica enclave, systematically shelling the overcrowded town. Thousands of refugees huddle in schools and public buildings as artillery rounds fall indiscriminately. General Morillon's dramatic personal guarantee becomes a symbol of the UN's agonizing position.
source_note: Existing Srebrenica arc sources ground the row's siege and humanitarian context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effects.text: Srebrenica is bombarded relentlessly. International outcry mounts as the enclave's humanitarian situation deteriorates.

title: Vance-Owen: Mostar Records Its Posture
narrative: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan was presented at Geneva on 2 January 1993 — a ten-province framework that ratifies three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) under the constitutional architecture of a decentralized Bosnia. Mate Boban signed the agreed text for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at Athens on 25 March 1993, with Tudjman's directive transmitted via the Granic-Susak channel: the provincial allocation is the operative territorial basis for HZ HB. The Mostar Presidency must record its posture toward the VOPP framework — accept the ten-province map, reject the plan and break with Zagreb's directive, condition acceptance on amendments, or condition acceptance on a reciprocal ARBiH signature.

effect.text: The HZ HB Presidency records its posture toward the Vance-Owen ten-province framework.

source_note: The Vance-Owen Peace Plan was presented at Geneva on 2 January 1993; Mate Boban signed for HZ HB at Athens on 25 March 1993, codifying three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) under the decentralized constitutional architecture. Sources: David Owen, Balkan Odyssey (Harcourt 1995) Ch. 4-5 (VOPP presentation 2 January 1993; Athens signature 25 March 1993; Boban posture); UN S/25221 (29 January 1993, Co-Chairmen's transmission of the VOPP framework) + UN S/25403 (12 March 1993, agreed text including provincial map Annex II); UN S/25479 (8 April 1993, Co-Chairmen's letter transmitting the agreed VOPP); ICTY Prlic et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment (29 May 2013) Vol. 3 §§412-498 (Tudjman Presidential Transcripts on HZ HB VOPP directive; Granic-Susak channel) and Vol. 1 §§452-470 (HR HB VOPP acceptance posture); Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlic Vol. 3 (Zagreb directive to Boban); Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II Ch. 3-5 (March-May 1993 chronology; HR HB Vance-Owen posture via Zagreb channel; provincial allocation favoring Croat claims). The X2 packet completes the Vance-Owen cross-faction trio: B3 (`vance_owen_plan_1993`) RBiH side; this row HRHB side; `rs_assembly_rejects_voplan_1993` RS side (Pale Assembly rejection May 1993). All three are gated on `vance_owen_plan_1993` (the RBiH-side row authored at turn 39 in this file functions as the cross-faction VOPP framework anchor) and on the responding faction's foundational flag (X1 London Conference / X3 Owen-Stoltenberg / X4 Contact Group cross-faction pattern from Packets 6/25/28). §3.6 forward-looking guard: any future `csq_hrhb_vance_owen_*` row consuming this row's outcomes MUST NOT re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, hostage-taking, civilian-targeting, paramilitary deployment, or any sensitive-act response option. The HRHB Vance-Owen acceptance led historically to the April 1993 Gornji Vakuf clashes and the April-October 1993 Lasva Valley atrocities, so consequence rows must stay within constitutional/political-strategic scope; central Bosnia HVO-ARBiH operations and any associated atrocity surfaces (Ahmici, Stupni Do, central-Bosnia detention camps, Mostar siege) remain canon-gated through their existing event surfaces (h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities; hrhb_camp_exposure; h8_mostar_bridge family slugs; gornji_vakuf_clashes_1993; ahmici_massacre_1993; croat_bosniak_war_begins_1993). Engine vocabulary substitutions per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md: Zagreb patron-confidence collapse on reject counterfactual captured via `patron_confidence -25`; Federation alliance break captured via `alliance_change +0.10` on the condition_on_arbih_reciprocity counterfactual (joint front overture) and `alliance_change -0.10` on reject; international-standing penalty per X1 London / X3 Owen-Stoltenberg pattern.
staff_assessment: Acceptance is the documented Mate Boban posture and Tudjman's directive — the ten-province map ratifies three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) under a decentralized Bosnia. Rejection breaks with Zagreb's directive and incurs a Tudjman patron-confidence collapse plus an alliance break with RBiH. Accept-with-modifications preserves the patron channel at a smaller patron-confidence cost. Condition-on-ARBiH-reciprocity opens a paradoxical joint-front overture: if Sarajevo signs simultaneously, the central-Bosnia friction can be contained — but Zagreb's patron-confidence falls when the HZ HB Presidency conditions signature on a Bosniak counter-signature rather than transmitting the directive cleanly.
trigger_evidence: The Vance-Owen Plan has been presented (per vance_owen_plan_1993, turn 39).
Mate Boban signed the agreed text for HZ HB at Athens on 25 March 1993.
Tudjman has directed the HZ HB Presidency to record the acceptance posture (Prlic Vol. 3 §§412-498).

response_options.label: Accept the Vance-Owen ten-province framework
response_options.description: Acknowledge the VOPP map: three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) are ratified inside the decentralized Bosnia framework. Mate Boban signs for HZ HB at Athens; Zagreb's directive is honored.

response_options.label: Condition acceptance on provincial-boundary amendments
response_options.description: Acknowledge the ten-province framework but condition the signature on amendments to the Central Bosnia and Western Herzegovina provincial boundaries. Zagreb tolerates the conditional posture without full alignment; the central-Bosnia frictions remain unresolved.

response_options.label: Condition signature on reciprocal ARBiH acceptance
response_options.description: Sign the VOPP framework only if Sarajevo signs simultaneously. A paradoxical joint-front overture: the central-Bosnia friction can be contained if Sarajevo reciprocates, but Zagreb reads the conditional signature as deferring patron direction to a Bosniak counter-signature rather than transmitting it cleanly.

response_options.label: Reject the Vance-Owen ten-province framework
response_options.description: Refuse the VOPP map. The HZ HB Presidency defies Zagreb's directive — Tudjman's patron-confidence collapses, the alliance with RBiH breaks further, and international standing falls. The central-Bosnia war continues without a settlement frame; the Croat-majority provinces remain a contested claim rather than a ratified allocation.

RBiH.headline: Mostar signs Vance-Owen at Athens
RBiH.body: HRHB acknowledges the Vance-Owen ten-province framework. Sarajevo reads the move as Zagreb-directed partition consolidation; three Croat-majority provinces (Mostar, Central Bosnia, Western Herzegovina) are ratified, and the central-Bosnia friction over the provincial allocation continues without a joint-front settlement.

RS.headline: Boban signs Vance-Owen for HZ HB
RS.body: HRHB accepts the Vance-Owen framework. Pale sees the second signature on a partition map and weighs the Pale Assembly's pending response toward the same framework.

RBiH.headline: Mostar conditions Vance-Owen signature
RBiH.body: HRHB signs the ten-province framework with Central Bosnia and Western Herzegovina boundary amendments. Sarajevo sees the patron channel hold tactically while local provincial-boundary disputes remain unresolved.

RS.headline: HZ HB signs Vance-Owen with amendments
RS.body: Mostar acknowledges the ten-province framework while conditioning signature on provincial-boundary amendments. Pale sees the partition map advance with internal HR HB-RBiH friction still in play.

RBiH.headline: Mostar conditions signature on Sarajevo reciprocity
RBiH.body: HRHB ties its Vance-Owen signature to a reciprocal ARBiH acceptance. Sarajevo reads the move as a paradoxical joint-front overture: the central-Bosnia friction can be contained if Sarajevo signs simultaneously, but the conditional signature defers patron direction to a Bosniak counter-signature.

RS.headline: HZ HB ties signature to ARBiH reciprocity
RS.body: Mostar conditions its Vance-Owen signature on Sarajevo signing simultaneously. Pale reads the move as a Croat-Bosniak coordination signal under the ten-province framework.

RBiH.headline: Mostar rejects Vance-Owen
RBiH.body: HRHB refuses the Vance-Owen framework despite Tudjman's directive. Sarajevo reads the move as a patron-channel rupture on the Croat side; the alliance falls further as the central-Bosnia war continues without a settlement frame.

RS.headline: HZ HB defies Zagreb on Vance-Owen
RS.body: Mostar rejects the ten-province framework despite Tudjman's directive. Pale reads the move as patron-channel rupture on the Croat side and weighs its own posture without the second signature.

title: UN Resolution 816 — No-Fly Zone Enforcement
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 816, authorizing member states to enforce the no-fly zone over Bosnia-Herzegovina that had been violated over 500 times since its establishment in October 1992. On April 12 NATO commences Operation Deny Flight with combat air patrols, marking a shift from passive monitoring to active military involvement.

effects.text: NATO combat aircraft now patrol Bosnian airspace. The VRS loses its fixed-wing air support but retains overwhelming ground-based fire superiority.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 816 (1993), S/RES/816. Operation Deny Flight USAF history.

title: Central Bosnia Pocket: HZ HB Records Its Defense Posture
narrative: The ARBiH-HVO war that erupted from the Gornji Vakuf clashes (Jan 1993, H2) has now boiled over across central Bosnia. The HVO holds three encircled pockets — the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle in the Lasva Valley, the Žepče exclave further north, and Mostar (west bank) — surrounded by ARBiH 3rd and 7th Corps formations whose strength dwarfs the local HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia. The triangle is operationally indefensible long-term: only a tenuous Croatia-routed airbridge through Tudjman's Susak channel sustains ammunition, fuel, and officer rotation into the pocket. Tihofil Blaškić commands the Operative Zone from Kiseljak; Dario Kordić leads HVO political affairs in central Bosnia. Mate Boban must record HZ HB's posture: defend the pocket (the documented historical posture — hold the triangle and Žepče through the airbridge until a diplomatic resolution arrives); evacuate to Herzegovina (cede the Croat heartland, withdraw forces along the corridor); attempt a breakout offensive (high casualty cost, near-certain failure against 3rd/7th Corps encirclement); or pursue early federation with RBiH (parallel to but distinct from the Feb 1994 Zagreb-ordered ceasefire — an April 1993 Croat-Bosniak federation overture against Tudjman's directive).

effect.text: Mostar records its posture toward the Central Bosnia pocket defense decision as the ARBiH-HVO war envelops the Lasva Valley triangle.

source_note: The April-October 1993 Central Bosnia pocket defense is one of the war's defining operational decisions on the HRHB side. After the Gornji Vakuf clashes (Jan 1993, H2) escalated into the full ARBiH-HVO war through spring 1993, HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia (Blaškić) held three encircled pockets: (i) the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle in the Lasva Valley anchoring the historical Croat heartland of central Bosnia, (ii) the Žepče exclave to the north (HVO Operative Group Žepče), and (iii) Mostar west bank under HVO Mostar. ARBiH 3rd Corps (Hadžihasanović) and 7th Corps (Alagić) operated the encirclement; the HVO pocket's local strength was a fraction of the ARBiH force ratio. The pocket was operationally indefensible long-term in pure force-correlation terms, but held through October 1993-March 1994 via the Croatia-routed airbridge (Tudjman-Susak channel; Pleso-Posušje-Kiseljak resupply axis; HV officer rotation; ammunition and fuel sustainment). The Washington Agreement of 18 March 1994 resolved the pocket through diplomatic federation rather than military defeat. Sources: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II (CIA Office of Russian and European Analysis 2002) chs. on April 1993-March 1994 ARBiH-HVO war chronology, HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia, Lasva Valley operations, Žepče exclave defense; ICTY Kordić & Čerkez IT-95-14/2-T Trial Judgment (26 February 2001) on HVO political leadership of central Bosnia (Kordić-Blaškić-Kraljević command coordination, Operative Zone Central Bosnia structure 1992-1994); ICTY Blaškić IT-95-14-T Trial Judgment (3 March 2000) on Operative Zone Central Bosnia operations through 1993-1994; ICTY Prlić et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment (29 May 2013) Vol. 1 §§591-640 and Vol. 3 §§412-498 on the Susak-Tudjman correspondence ratifying the airbridge sustainment channel; ICTY Naletilić & Martinović IT-98-34-T Trial Judgment on the Mostar siege axis (separate from the central-Bosnia pocket but operationally adjacent); Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3 on the directive to sustain the pocket via Croatia. §3.6 STRICT FORWARD-LOOKING GUARD (Lasva Valley sensitive-history canon-gate): the April-October 1993 central-Bosnia operations included the Ahmici massacre (16 April 1993 — ICTY Kupreškić et al. IT-95-16-T + Blaškić + Kordić & Čerkez), Stupni Do (23 October 1993 — ICTY Rajić IT-95-12 + Prlić Vol. 2), and other ICTY-litigated atrocities across the Lasva Valley and Vareš axis. THE H6 DECISION IS OPERATIONAL (defend triangle / evacuate / breakout / federate_early) NOT ATROCITY-COUPLED. Consequence chain prohibitions binding on ALL csq_hrhb_central_bosnia_* descendants: (a) defend_pocket MUST NOT be rewarded with cleansing/displacement/civilian-targeting/paramilitary-deployment effects; (b) Ahmici/Stupni Do/Vitez detention/Lasva Valley atrocity rows MUST NOT appear as downstream choices reachable from any H6 option; (c) NO consequence row may open paramilitary-deployment, civilian-targeting, forced-displacement, ethnic-targeting, hostage-taking, detention-camp-expansion, or any sensitive-act response option in any csq_hrhb_central_bosnia_* descendant. The sensitive Lasva Valley / Stupni Do history is canonical fact but stays canon-gated through the existing event surfaces (h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities family, h8_mostar_bridge family, hrhb_camp_exposure / hrhb_detention_camp_exposure family slugs already registered in RING3_SENSITIVE_FAMILIES per src/sim/events/event_families.ts). Cost-floor topology reflects the operational stakes: defend_pocket (historical) carries POSITIVE airbridge-sustained operational morale (morale_change +2 + patron_confidence +5 + military_credibility +5 + internal_cohesion +3 — pocket held the Croat heartland through diplomatic resolution); evacuate_to_herzegovina (counterfactual) carries severe territorial-legitimacy collapse (alliance_change +0.10 de-escalation but territorial_legitimacy -30 loss of historical Croat central-Bosnia heartland + internal_cohesion -25 Vitez/Travnik Croat communities displaced + patron_confidence -15 Tudjman opposed pocket abandonment); breakout_offensive (counterfactual) carries high casualty cost and near-certain failure against ARBiH 3rd/7th Corps encirclement (alliance_change -0.10 amplified rupture + military_credibility -15 historical record shows breakout would have failed + recruitment_modifier 0.85x × 6 turns); federate_early (counterfactual) — parallel to H4 (Zagreb-ordered ceasefire Feb 1994, `zagreb_orders_hrhb_ceasefire`) but at PACKET-EARLIER timing (April 1993 federation overture against Tudjman's directive) — carries paradoxical de-escalation gain at patron-channel rupture (alliance_change +0.15 strong Federation overture + patron_confidence -25 Tudjman opposed the early federation + negotiating_leverage +10). Note: federate_early effects DELIBERATELY DIFFER from H4 effects to capture the EARLIER counterfactual road-not-taken (April 1993 vs Feb 1994). Engine vocabulary substitutions per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md: alliance_change captures the RBiH↔HRHB Federation alliance proxy; patron_confidence captures the Zagreb relationship; territorial_legitimacy captures the loss-of-Croat-heartland proxy on evacuate_to_herzegovina; recruitment_modifier captures the casualty-cost manpower constriction on breakout_offensive (subject to memory/recruitment_modifier_dead_channel.md caveat — narrative effect is independent of whether the modifier propagates to brigade pool). This packet extends the HRHB chain (H1) by one downstream event (was 10, now 11 in `enables_events_runtime`).
staff_assessment: Defending the pocket is the documented Mostar posture across the April 1993-March 1994 window: Boban, Blaškić, Kordić, and the HZ HB Presidency aligned that holding the Lasva Valley triangle and Žepče exclave through the Tudjman-Susak airbridge channel was operationally sustainable until a diplomatic resolution arrived. Evacuation is the maximum-cost counterfactual on identity/territorial-legitimacy grounds — surrendering the historical Croat heartland of central Bosnia would collapse the HZ HB territorial claim and displace Vitez/Travnik Croat communities under ARBiH control. Breakout is the maximum-cost counterfactual on military grounds — the force ratio against ARBiH 3rd/7th Corps made any breakout operationally near-certain to fail, with casualty losses that would dwarf the airbridge-sustained holding pattern. Federate_early is the road-not-taken counterfactual at the patron-channel cost — an April 1993 federation overture would have anticipated the Washington Agreement framework by eleven months but at the cost of a Tudjman patron-channel rupture (Zagreb opposed the early federation; the Croat-Bosniak war had to run its course before Tudjman's Susak channel could be diverted to compliance with the Granic-Silajdzic Washington track). The historical default reflects the operational reality: the pocket was sustainable via the airbridge until diplomatic resolution.
trigger_evidence: The ARBiH-HVO war from spring 1993 has encircled HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia in the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle plus the Žepče exclave.
ARBiH 3rd Corps (Hadžihasanović) and 7th Corps (Alagić) hold the encirclement with a force ratio favorable to ARBiH.
The Tudjman-Susak airbridge channel sustains the pocket via Croatia routing — operationally viable but politically conditional on Zagreb's continued patronage.

response_options.label: Defend the pocket
response_options.description: Hold the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle and the Žepče exclave. Blaškić consolidates the Operative Zone defenses; the Tudjman-Susak airbridge sustains ammunition, fuel, and officer rotation through Croatia. The pocket is operationally viable until a diplomatic resolution arrives — the Croat heartland of central Bosnia is preserved on the ground.

response_options.label: Evacuate to Herzegovina
response_options.description: Withdraw HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia along the corridor to Herzegovina. The Lasva Valley triangle and Žepče exclave are abandoned; Vitez, Busovaca, Kiseljak, Travnik, and Žepče Croat communities are displaced under ARBiH control. The ARBiH-HVO war de-escalates dramatically — a Croat-Bosniak alliance reconstruction becomes structurally easier — but the historical Croat heartland of central Bosnia is surrendered. Tudjman is furious: pocket abandonment was politically forbidden in his directive.

response_options.label: Mount a breakout offensive
response_options.description: Launch HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia in a coordinated breakout offensive against the ARBiH 3rd Corps encirclement. The force ratio is heavily unfavorable; the historical record across the April 1993-October 1993 window shows ARBiH 3rd/7th Corps strength would have absorbed and crushed any breakout attempt before it could reach Operative Zone South-East Herzegovina relief axes. Heavy casualties drain the HVO manpower pool; the airbridge sustainment is squandered on a militarily near-impossible operation.

response_options.label: Federate early with RBiH
response_options.description: Open an April 1993 federation overture with Sarajevo — eleven months ahead of the historical Washington Agreement (Mar 1994). HZ HB Presidency formally proposes federated HVO-ARBiH command coordination, ceasefire across central Bosnia, and joint anti-VRS prosecution. Tudjman is opposed: Zagreb's directive across spring 1993 was pocket-hold, not federation-early; the patron-channel ruptures. Negotiating leverage at the international table rises sharply — Mostar anticipates the Washington framework. This is the road-not-taken counterfactual distinct from H4 (zagreb_orders_hrhb_ceasefire, Feb 1994).

RBiH.headline: HVO digs in to hold central-Bosnia pocket
RBiH.body: Mostar orders Blaškić to consolidate the Vitez/Busovaca/Kiseljak triangle and the Žepče exclave. Sarajevo reads the airbridge sustainment as politically conditional but operationally durable; the central-Bosnia front hardens through 1993.

RS.headline: HVO sustains central-Bosnia defensive pockets
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna consolidates HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia defense through the Croatia airbridge. Pale reads the ARBiH-HVO war as locked into prolonged attrition; the partition map favors Pale's diplomatic position.

RBiH.headline: HVO withdraws from central-Bosnia heartland
RBiH.body: Mostar orders HVO Operative Zone Central Bosnia to withdraw along the corridor to Herzegovina. Sarajevo reads the dramatic de-escalation in central Bosnia but inherits responsibility for Vitez/Travnik Croat communities — the ARBiH-HVO war winds down at the cost of HZ HB's territorial claim.

RS.headline: HVO abandons central-Bosnia pockets
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna withdraws HVO forces from central Bosnia to Herzegovina. Pale reads the territorial concession to ARBiH but notes the Tudjman patron-channel friction; the partition map is reshaped by Croat retreat.

RBiH.headline: HVO mounts central-Bosnia breakout attempt
RBiH.body: Mostar orders Blaškić to mount a coordinated breakout offensive from the Lasva Valley triangle. Sarajevo reads the desperate operational gamble; 3rd Corps and 7th Corps are repositioned to absorb the breakout. Casualties mount on both sides.

RS.headline: HVO launches doomed central-Bosnia breakout
RS.body: Herceg-Bosna mounts a breakout offensive against ARBiH 3rd Corps encirclement. Pale reads the force-ratio mismatch and the predictable casualty cost; the ARBiH-HVO war escalates while VRS holds its main axes.

RBiH.headline: Mostar proposes early federation with Sarajevo
RBiH.body: HZ HB Presidency opens an April 1993 federation overture — eleven months ahead of the Washington framework. Sarajevo reads the Croat-Bosniak war ending earlier than history records, but notes Zagreb's patron-channel rupture as the operational cost of the diplomatic gain.

RS.headline: Herceg-Bosna federates early with Sarajevo
RS.body: Mostar opens federation talks with Sarajevo in spring 1993, eleven months ahead of the historical Washington track. Pale reads the Croat-Bosniak realignment against partition framing and notes the Tudjman patron-channel rupture as the leading indicator.

ICTY Kordić & Čerkez IT-95-14/2-T Trial Judgment (26 February 2001) §§465-650 — HVO political leadership of central Bosnia, Operative Zone Central Bosnia command structure 1992-1994. ICTY Blaškić IT-95-14-T Trial Judgment (3 March 2000) §§99-220 — Operative Zone Central Bosnia operations 1993. ICTY Prlić et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment (29 May 2013) Vol. 1 §§591-640 and Vol. 3 §§412-498 — Tudjman-Susak correspondence on the airbridge sustainment channel. Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3 — directive to sustain the pocket via Croatia. ICTY Naletilić & Martinović IT-98-34-T Trial Judgment — Mostar siege axis context.

title: Croatia Tightens Control over Herceg-Bosna
narrative: The Republic of Croatia deepens its de facto control over the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna: HV officers serve in HVO command positions, Croatian state resources flow across the border, and Zagreb's directives increasingly drive HVO military strategy. The ICTY Prlic trial establishes a Joint Criminal Enterprise involving Tudjman's inner circle and HVO commanders aimed at creating ethnically homogeneous Croat territory for eventual annexation.

effects.text: Zagreb's patronage deepens. HVO commanders receive Croatian Army support — and with it, the expectation that Herceg-Bosna will serve Croatian strategic interests.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), JCE findings. ICTY Appeals Judgment (IT-04-74-A).

title: Sovici-Doljani Attack
narrative: HVO forces attack the Bosniak villages of Sovici and Doljani near Jablanica, detaining approximately 400 Bosniak civilians and capturing 70-75 ARBiH soldiers. The attack occurs simultaneously with the Ahmici massacre in the Lasva Valley, revealing coordinated HVO operations across both central Bosnia and Herzegovina.

effects.text: Coordinated HVO operations strike from Jablanica to the Lasva Valley simultaneously. The scale reveals systematic planning behind what the HVO publicly frames as defensive action.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), Vol. 2. ICTY Naletilic-Martinovic Trial Judgment (IT-98-34-T).

title: Trusina Killings
narrative: ARBiH forces kill 15 Croat civilians and 7 HVO prisoners of war in the village of Trusina near Konjic, on the same day as the Ahmici massacre. The reciprocal atrocities illustrate the descending cycle of ethnic violence that the Croat-Bosniak war has unleashed across central Bosnia.

effects.text: War crimes on both sides deepen mutual hatred. Each atrocity becomes justification for the next.

historical_source: Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Case S1 1 K 017327 16 Kre2.

title: UN Resolution 819 — Srebrenica Safe Area
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 819, declaring Srebrenica a 'safe area' free from armed attack or any hostile act, and demanding an immediate VRS ceasefire and unimpeded humanitarian access. The declaration creates a promise of protection without committing the military means to enforce it.
source_note: UNSCR 819 grounds the row's safe-area mandate and diplomatic context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effects.text: Srebrenica is declared a UN safe area. The VRS ignores the ceasefire demand while the UN lacks any credible enforcement mechanism.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 819 (1993), S/RES/819.

title: UN Resolution 820 — Tightened Sanctions on Serbia
narrative: The Security Council passes Resolution 820, substantially reinforcing the sanctions regime against Serbia and Montenegro. Following the Bosnian Serb assembly's rejection of the Vance-Owen plan on April 26, all commodity transport across Serbian borders is prohibited except medical supplies and foodstuffs, further strangling the RS supply chain through its patron.

effects.text: The tightened embargo enters force. Belgrade's ability to sustain the VRS is visibly constrained, and Milosevic's patience with Pale is running thin.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 820 (1993), S/RES/820.

title: Srebrenica Demilitarization Agreement
narrative: Under intense international pressure following the VRS assault on Srebrenica, Generals Mladic and Halilovic sign a demilitarization agreement on April 17-18: the ARBiH is to surrender weapons under UNPROFOR supervision in exchange for a ceasefire and UN troop deployment. Implementation is flawed on both sides — the ARBiH hides weapons while the VRS continues to restrict humanitarian convoys.
source_note: ICTY Krstic and the Halilovic-Mladic agreement ground the row's demilitarization context. Per UN A/54/549 (Secretary-General's report on the fall of Srebrenica, 15 November 1999), paragraphs 57-98, and ICTY Krstic IT-98-33-T paragraphs 16-28, fuller compliance under hollow UN protection historically INCREASED enclave vulnerability. The enclave_resilience direction on comply_fully reflects this empirical history, consistent with SENSITIVE_HISTORY_DESIGN_GATE Ring 3 item 10 (no gamified atrocity-prevention surface; the only outcome is the absence of a genocide_condemnation flag). This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effect.text: The demilitarization agreement is signed. Srebrenica is technically disarmed — but both sides are already maneuvering around its terms.

response_options.label: Comply in appearance, hide weapons
response_options.description: Surrender visible stocks while concealing reserves. The historical choice — preserving minimum defense capability.

response_options.label: Comply fully with disarmament
response_options.description: Surrender all weapons as demanded. Gains international credibility but leaves the enclave with no combat-effective defensive capability under continued VRS pressure.

response_options.label: Refuse disarmament
response_options.description: Publicly reject the agreement. Maintains military capability but repudiates the UN safe-area framework and draws international condemnation and increased VRS pressure.

RS.headline: RBiH accepts Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders accept full weapons surrender under UNPROFOR supervision. Pale sees Sarajevo gaining mediator credibility while the enclave's defense becomes more exposed.

HRHB.headline: RBiH accepts Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders accept full weapons surrender under UNPROFOR supervision. Mostar sees Sarajevo trading enclave military capacity for stronger standing with international mediators.

RS.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Pale sees formal compliance language paired with an effort to keep minimum defense capability inside the enclave.

HRHB.headline: RBiH hedges Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders surrender visible stocks while preserving hidden reserves. Mostar sees Sarajevo trying to satisfy UNPROFOR supervision without leaving the enclave fully exposed.

RS.headline: RBiH rejects Srebrenica disarmament
RS.body: RBiH commanders reject the demilitarization terms and keep the enclave armed. Pale sees preserved military capability at the cost of international condemnation and renewed pressure.

HRHB.headline: RBiH rejects Srebrenica disarmament
HRHB.body: RBiH commanders reject the demilitarization terms and keep the enclave armed. Mostar sees Sarajevo accepting diplomatic damage to avoid surrendering the enclave's remaining defense.

historical_source: UN A/54/549 (Secretary-General's report on the fall of Srebrenica, 15 November 1999), §§57-98 — partial/nominal compliance pattern. UN Security Council Resolution 819 (16 April 1993) declaring Srebrenica a safe area. Demilitarization Agreement of 18 April 1993 (Sarajevo airport, UN-brokered); Demilitarization Agreement of 8 May 1993 (Žepa extension). ICTY Krstić Trial Judgement (IT-98-33-T, 2 August 2001), §§16-28 — 1993 background narrative. General Philippe Morillon's visit to Srebrenica, 11 March 1993.

title: UN Declares Safe Areas
narrative: The UN Security Council passes Resolution 819, declaring Srebrenica a safe area, followed by Resolution 824 extending protection to Sarajevo, Tuzla, Zepa, Gorazde, and Bihac. The resolutions promise protection without committing adequate military force to deliver it — a fatal gap between mandate and means that will have catastrophic consequences.

effects.text: Six UN safe areas are declared. The promise of protection raises hope among besieged populations, but no credible enforcement mechanism exists.

title: Milošević Orders Karadžić: Accept Vance-Owen
narrative: Milošević and Bulatović fly to Zvornik to personally demand that the Bosnian Serb Assembly accept the Vance-Owen Plan. Belgrade cannot sustain UN sanctions indefinitely — Pale's intransigence is destroying Serbia's economy.

effect.text: Milošević and Bulatović personally demand that the Bosnian Serb Assembly accept the Vance-Owen Plan.

title: Vitez-Kiseljak Pockets Isolated
narrative: As the Croat-Bosniak war intensifies, HVO garrisons in the Vitez-Busovaca pocket and the Kiseljak enclave become increasingly cut off from resupply by HVO main forces in western Herzegovina. The pockets must survive on local resources and intermittent VRS cooperation, while the ARBiH weighs the cost of an assault against the benefits of encirclement.

effects.text: HVO defenders in central Bosnia fight with the desperation of encirclement. Each convoy that fails to reach them deepens the crisis.

historical_source: ICTY Kordic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14/2-T). ICTY Blaskic Trial Judgment (IT-95-14-T).

title: Bosnian Serb Assembly Rejects Vance-Owen Plan
narrative: Despite Karadzic's signature on the Vance-Owen plan at Athens on May 2 (under Greek and FRY pressure, with the explicit condition of RS Assembly ratification), the Republika Srpska National Assembly convenes at Bijeljina on May 5-6 and votes to reject the plan. General Mladic presents maps arguing the territorial allocation is militarily unacceptable. Despite Milosevic's personal intervention (with Bulatovic, Cosic, and Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis), the Assembly refers the decision to a referendum. The 15-16 May referendum produces a 96% rejection. Lord Owen declares the plan dead on June 18 — the last comprehensive peace proposal that preserved a unified Bosnia has failed.
source_note: Karadzic judgment and RS Assembly proceedings summarize the Pale rejection of Vance-Owen and the follow-on referendum.
staff_assessment: Pale leadership can preserve assembly cohesion by accepting the rejection, but doing so deepens patron pressure and leaves the international plan dead.
trigger_evidence: Vance-Owen has already been presented in the event chain.
The RS Assembly rejected the plan at Pale after Karadzic's signature.

effect.text: The Assembly has spoken. The Vance-Owen plan is dead. The war continues on Pale's terms.

response_options.label: Accept the assembly's vote
response_options.description: The people have spoken. Reject international pressure and continue the war. Internal cohesion is preserved but Serbia is furious.

future_consequences.label: Vance-Owen rejection stands
future_consequences.explanation: Accepting the assembly vote does not open or close catalog events by metadata; it makes the political cost branch visible through the existing RS morale and patron-pressure effects. Karadžić IT-95-5/18-T §§3526-3530 records the Pale leadership's acquiescence in the Bijeljina rejection despite the Athens 2 May signature.

response_options.label: Attempt to override the assembly
response_options.description: Defy the nationalist vote and push for acceptance. Historically impossible — risks fracturing the RS political structure.

future_consequences.label: Assembly override risk
future_consequences.explanation: Attempting to override the assembly does not open or close catalog events by metadata; it makes the internal-fracture branch visible through the existing RS morale and patron-pressure effects. Krajišnik IT-00-39-T §§995-1019 records the SDS Assembly architecture and the leadership's structural deference; override fractures the legitimating institution at the cost-floor levels documented in the R7 worksheet (internal_cohesion ≤-15, patron_confidence ≤-20).

HRHB.headline: Pale accepts the assembly rejection
HRHB.body: Republika Srpska accepts the Pale assembly vote against Vance-Owen and continues the war. HVO leaders see RS internal cohesion preserved while Belgrade's anger and international isolation grow.

RBiH.headline: RS assembly rejection stands
RBiH.body: Republika Srpska accepts the assembly's rejection of Vance-Owen. Sarajevo sees the comprehensive peace proposal fail while Pale preserves cohesion and absorbs heavier outside pressure.

HRHB.headline: Pale tries to override its assembly
HRHB.body: Republika Srpska leadership attempts to push acceptance despite the assembly vote. HVO staff see improved diplomatic posture for Pale, but a serious fracture inside RS politics.

RBiH.headline: RS leadership challenges the assembly vote
RBiH.body: Republika Srpska tries to override the nationalist rejection of Vance-Owen. Sarajevo sees a possible diplomatic opening, paired with visible strain in Pale's political structure.

historical_source: ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T, 24 March 2016) paras. 3251-3268 (FRY/Greek pressure for acceptance), 3447 (Karadzic pattern of sign-internationally / reject-domestically), 3471-3475 (Six Strategic Goals incompatibility with VOPP), 3526-3530 (Athens signature 2 May 1993, Bijeljina rejection 5-6 May 1993, referendum 15-16 May, Owen declaration 18 June). ICTY Mladic Trial Judgment (IT-09-92-T, 22 November 2017) paras. 3232-3243 (Mladic maps presented to the Assembly). ICTY Krajisnik Trial Judgment (IT-00-39-T, 27 September 2006) paras. 856-891 (Assembly proceedings, Krajisnik as Assembly President). Vance-Owen Peace Plan text: UN S/25221 (11 February 1993). UN Security Council Resolution 820 (17 April 1993). Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II pp. 9-32, 28-31.

title: ICTY Formally Established — Resolution 827
narrative: The UN Security Council unanimously passes Resolution 827, formally establishing the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia — the first war crimes court created by the UN since Nuremberg and Tokyo. The tribunal has jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, and violations of the laws of war committed in the former Yugoslavia since 1991. While indictments are years away, the era of impunity may be ending.

effects.text: The ICTY opens for business in The Hague. Every commander who orders atrocities now does so with knowledge that a court exists to try them.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 827 (1993), S/RES/827.

title: Battle of Travnik — ARBiH Recaptures City
narrative: The ARBiH 3rd Corps launches an offensive against HVO positions in Travnik, overwhelming the garrison within days. Thousands of Croat civilians flee across VRS lines rather than remain under ARBiH control. The loss of Travnik is a major setback for the HVO in central Bosnia, demonstrating the ARBiH's growing numerical superiority in the interior.

effects.text: Travnik falls to the ARBiH. Croat civilians flee, and the HVO's position in central Bosnia begins its terminal decline.

historical_source: ICTY Hadzihasanovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-47-T).

title: Operation Neretva '93
narrative: The ARBiH launches Operation Neretva '93 against HVO positions in Herzegovina and the Neretva Valley. The offensive aims to break the HVO siege of East Mostar and secure a corridor to the coast. Fierce fighting erupts around Jablanica and along the Neretva River as the ARBiH attempts to exploit its growing numerical advantage.

effect.text: The ARBiH launches Operation Neretva '93, striking at HVO positions in the Neretva Valley and around Mostar.

title: UN Resolution 836 — Use of Force Authorized
narrative: The Security Council passes Resolution 836, authorizing UNPROFOR to use force in reply to bombardments against safe areas and permitting member states to use 'all necessary measures through the use of air power' in and around them. This is the legal foundation for future NATO air strikes — though the dual-key arrangement between the UN and NATO means the authorization exists largely on paper.

effects.text: NATO now has legal authority to strike VRS positions. Whether it has the political will to use it is another question entirely.

historical_source: UN Security Council Resolution 836 (1993), S/RES/836.

title: Operation Sharp Guard — NATO Naval Blockade
narrative: NATO and the Western European Union begin Operation Sharp Guard, a combined naval blockade in the Adriatic Sea to enforce UN sanctions against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the arms embargo on all former Yugoslav republics. The operation intercepts merchant shipping, tightening the economic noose on Serbia while limiting — though not eliminating — arms flows to all parties.

effects.text: NATO warships enforce the Adriatic blockade. Serbia's supply corridor tightens further, but the arms embargo continues to hurt the outgunned ARBiH most.

historical_source: NATO Operation Sharp Guard records. UN Security Council sanctions monitoring reports.

title: HVO Detention Camps Established
narrative: Following the eruption of full-scale Croat-Bosniak war, HVO forces conduct mass arrests of Bosniak men across Herzegovina, including Bosniak members of the HVO itself. Thousands are held in a network of camps including Dretelj Prison, Gabela, and the Heliodrom complex near Mostar. Conditions are brutal — overcrowding, starvation, beatings, and forced labor — paralleling the Serb-run camps revealed at Omarska the previous year.

effects.text: Images of Bosniak men crowded behind Heliodrom wire reach the international press. Croatia's patron relationship with the West enters a period of severe strain.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T), Vol. 3. ICTY Naletilic-Martinovic Trial Judgment (IT-98-34-T).

title: Sarajevo Tunnel Completed
narrative: After four months of secret construction under the codename 'Objekt BD,' the 800-meter tunnel connecting besieged Dobrinja to free territory at Butmir — passing under the UN-controlled airport runway — is completed. The tunnel carries up to 20 tonnes of supplies daily: food, weapons, ammunition, and communications equipment. It transforms Sarajevo's siege from a total blockade into a strangled but survivable containment.

effects.text: Sarajevo breathes again. The tunnel is a military and psychological lifeline — proof that the city's will to resist can find a way through any encirclement.

historical_source: Sarajevo Tunnel Museum archives. ICTY Galic Trial Judgment (IT-98-29-T).

title: Operation Lukavac 93 — VRS Offensive on Igman
narrative: The VRS launches Operation Lukavac 93 with 15,000 troops against ARBiH positions on Mount Igman and Bjelasnica, aiming to sever Sarajevo's last supply route. VRS forces capture the Igman road on August 4, bringing the city to the brink of total isolation. The offensive provokes the first credible NATO threat of air strikes and a UN-brokered withdrawal demand.
source_note: Pascal, Balkan Battlegrounds II pp.410-411 frames Lukavac 93 as VRS pressure from Rogoj/Trnovo toward Igman and Bjelasnica after ARBiH Gorazde corridor pressure, threatening Sarajevo's supply link and creating the UN-NATO pressure path for withdrawal.
staff_assessment: The advance has created a local military gain, but holding Igman now risks converting a battlefield success into a direct confrontation with NATO and further patron pressure.
trigger_evidence: ARBiH pressure toward the Gorazde corridor has drawn VRS attention to the Rogoj-Trnovo axis.
RS control around Trnovo and pressure on Hadzici route proxies indicate a credible threat to the Igman-Bjelasnica supply link.
UN and NATO warnings are visible enough that withdrawal is a live political-military option, not a guaranteed outcome.

effect.text: VRS forces have seized the Igman road. Sarajevo faces total isolation — and NATO is issuing its first genuine ultimatum.

response_options.label: Comply with withdrawal demand
response_options.description: Pull back from Igman under the UN-brokered agreement. Avoids NATO strikes but concedes the strategic gain.

response_options.label: Defy NATO — hold Igman
response_options.description: Call NATO's bluff and hold the captured positions. Risks triggering the first NATO combat strikes in history.

RBiH.headline: VRS withdraws from Igman under pressure
RBiH.body: RS accepts the UN-brokered withdrawal demand after the Lukavac 93 advance. Sarajevo sees the immediate threat to the Igman route ease, while VRS gives up a strategic gain.

HRHB.headline: VRS complies on Igman withdrawal
HRHB.body: RS pulls back from the Igman positions rather than trigger NATO strikes. Mostar sees Western pressure contain the offensive, with VRS credibility taking a cost.

RBiH.headline: VRS defies NATO over Igman
RBiH.body: RS holds the captured Igman positions despite the threat of air strikes. Sarajevo faces renewed isolation pressure, while the risk of NATO combat action rises sharply.

HRHB.headline: VRS holds Igman against NATO warning
HRHB.body: RS calls the air-strike threat and keeps the Igman gains. Mostar sees stronger VRS battlefield posture, but also a more dangerous confrontation with NATO.

historical_source: ICTY Mladic Trial Judgment (IT-09-92-T). Washington Post, Aug 14 1993.

title: Maglaj Enclave Under Joint HVO-VRS Blockade
narrative: Following the collapse of the ARBiH-HVO alliance, the HVO joins the VRS in imposing a complete blockade on the Bosniak-held pocket around Maglaj, trapping approximately 100,000 people. The town endures relentless bombardment and near-total isolation for nine months, surviving partly on US airdrop supplies. The joint siege exemplifies the impossible tactical situation the ARBiH now faces — encircled from two directions simultaneously.

effects.text: Maglaj's joint blockade is a new strategic reality: the ARBiH must now defend against coordinated Serb and Croat pressure in the same valley.

historical_source: ICTY Prlic Trial Judgment (IT-04-74-T).

title: Mostar Records the Scope of Croat Territorial Claims
narrative: Summer 1993. The HZ HB controls its widest territorial footprint: Mostar west bank consolidated after the May rupture with ARBiH, Herzegovina core (Posušje, Grude, Ljubuški, Čitluk, Široki Brijeg, Tomislavgrad), the Central Bosnia pockets (Vitez-Busovača-Kiseljak triangle plus Žepče exclave), and a chain of sustaining checkpoints on the Tudjman-Susak airbridge. Mate Boban faces a foundational scope decision now that the territorial peak has been reached. The Presidency must record the operative claim posture for the Geneva, Owen-Stoltenberg, and downstream Contact Group / Washington / Dayton diplomatic tracks: keep the cantons-plus pragmatic-maximum framing the Vance-Owen and Owen-Stoltenberg plans ratify (Banovina-aligned but bounded), advance an expansive-conquest claim line that pushes for full "historical Croat lands" framing including eastern Herzegovina, formalize a Boban-Karadžić axis on the Graz 6 May 1992 partition logic against Sarajevo's central-Bosnia residual, or pull back to a minimum-consolidation footprint (Mostar plus western Herzegovina) and abandon the central-Bosnia pockets diplomatically.

effect.text: The HZ HB Presidency records the scope of its territorial claim for the Geneva and downstream diplomatic tracks.

source_note: Summer 1993 was the high-water mark of HZ HB territorial control: post-Mostar-rupture (9 May 1993 HVO west-bank consolidation per Prlić IT-04-74-T Vol. 2 §§240-330), Central Bosnia pocket consolidation across the Vitez-Busovača-Kiseljak triangle plus Žepče exclave (Prlić Vol. 1 §§591-640; Kordić & Čerkez IT-95-14/2-T §§465-650; Blaškić IT-95-14-T §§99-220), and the sustaining Tudjman-Susak airbridge to central Bosnia (Tudjman Presidential Transcripts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3). Mate Boban (HZ HB President until 8 February 1994 succession; replaced by Krešimir Zubak under Federation pressure on 5 August 1994) faced the foundational scope decision under sustained Tudjman pressure. Sources for the scope-decision frame: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II 1993 chronology (CIA Office of Russian and European Analysis 2002) — peak-territorial-reach window and HZ HB diplomatic posture; ICTY Prlić et al. IT-04-74-T Trial Judgment (29 May 2013) Vol. 1 §§423-590 (HZ HB founding 18 Nov 1991; HR HB proclamation 28 Aug 1993 — Republic upgrade falls inside this packet's window); Vol. 1 §§591-640 (Central Bosnia operative-zone posture); Vol. 2 §§240-330 (Mostar west-bank consolidation, May 1993); Vol. 3 §§412-498 (Tudjman Presidential Transcripts on HZ HB Vance-Owen and Owen-Stoltenberg directives, central-Bosnia airbridge correspondence, scope guidance through summer 1993); Prlić Appeals Judgment (29 November 2017) §§601-650 (JCE common purpose along 1939 Banovina lines — the canonical bounded-maximum scope template); ICTY Karadžić IT-95-5/18-T Vol. III on the Graz 6 May 1992 Boban-Karadžić joint statement and the partition logic; the Tudjman-Šušak correspondence excerpts admitted at Prlić Vol. 3 (scope-restraint memoranda spring-summer 1993); David Owen, Balkan Odyssey (Harcourt 1995) chs. 4-7 (Vance-Owen ten-province + Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics — the cantons-plus templates the pragmatic-maximum posture ratifies); Holbrooke, To End a War (Random House 1998) chs. 4-6 (Washington / Federation framework that closes the scope window at March 1994); Dayton General Framework Agreement (initialed 21 Nov 1995; Paris 14 Dec 1995) — Annex 4 BiH Constitution confirms the Federation footprint smaller than peak-1993 HZ HB control. §3.6 STRICT (sensitive-territory canon-gate prose — central safety constraint of this packet): the expansive_conquest and maximalist_with_serb_alliance counterfactuals are borderline sensitive territory. Cost floors MUST BE PUNITIVE on those branches and ARE PUNITIVE as authored: expansive_conquest carries international_standing -40 (UN/EC/EU recoil + UNSCR triple-sanctions threat per the Croatia sanctions architecture being signaled through 1993 - UNSCR 757/787/820 Yugoslavia-side parallel), alliance_change -0.20 (Federation-track foreclosed), patron_confidence -20 (Tudjman cautioned against open-conquest framing per Prlić Vol. 3 Tudjman-Šušak scope-restraint memoranda), recruitment_modifier 0.85x/8t (international-isolation supply cost), and negotiating_leverage -25 (Geneva/Owen-Stoltenberg/Contact-Group circuits narrow under sanctions-pressure framing); maximalist_with_serb_alliance carries the maximum-cost trio of alliance_change -0.30 (Federation-track foreclosed and amplified by Belgrade-axis signal), international_standing -50 (UNSCR triple-sanctions equivalent + EU recoil at Boban-Karadžić Graz axis formalization), patron_confidence -30 (Tudjman patron-channel rupture on open Belgrade-axis posture), and negotiating_leverage -40 (Geneva/Owen-Stoltenberg/Contact-Group circuits closed under the Graz-axis exposure framing). These cost floors are PUNITIVE - they NEVER reward expansive-conquest or Belgrade-axis posture with territorial gain or recruitment pool boost (the recruitment_modifier on expansive_conquest is a SUPPLY PENALTY at 0.85x, not a boost). Any future `csq_hrhb_territorial_*` consumer of this row's outcomes MUST NOT re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, civilian-targeting, paramilitary-deployment, ethnic-targeting, hostage-taking, detention-camp-expansion, or any sensitive-act response option. The sensitive history for HRHB territorial expansion - the Ahmici massacre (16 April 1993, Lašva Valley), the Stupni Do massacre (23 October 1993, Vareš), the broader Lašva Valley campaign (Vitez detention, Kaonik camp), the Mostar east-bank siege and the Stari Most destruction (9 November 1993), and the central-Bosnia HVO detention camps (Heliodrom, Dretelj, Gabela) - remains canon-gated through existing event surfaces: h5_croat_bosniak_war_atrocities (Lašva Valley + Stupni Do + Ahmici cluster), h8_mostar_bridge (Stari Most destruction + Mostar east-bank siege), hrhb_camp_exposure / hrhb_detention_camp_exposure (Heliodrom + Dretelj + Gabela + Vitez detention surface), and hrhb_mostar_bridge_destruction_1993 (Stari Most specifically). These are enumerated in RING3_SENSITIVE_FAMILIES per src/sim/events/event_families.ts. Any csq descendant of H40 MUST keep these slugs as the canonical surface; H40 itself authors only the diplomatic-scope posture decision (cantons-plus / expansive / Belgrade-axis / minimum-consolidation) and never the operational atrocity execution. Engine vocabulary substitutions per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md: alliance_lock(zagreb) -N collapses to patron_confidence -N; alliance_lock(rbih) ±N collapses to alliance_change ±N/10; recruitment_pool -15% on expansive_conquest collapses to recruitment_modifier 0.85x × 8t (multiplicative + duration); territorial_loss on minimum_consolidation collapses to territorial_legitimacy -25 (the canonical proxy delta - the engine has no flip-territory-on-decision surface for counterfactuals, per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md). New event reuses existing HRHB_BRANCH_TAGS entries (`hrhb_croat_republic` for pragmatic_maximum and expansive_conquest reflecting the Croat-Republic territorial frame across both options; `hrhb_strategic_ambiguity` for minimum_consolidation reflecting the dual-track abandonment of central-Bosnia pockets; `hrhb_friction_collapse` for maximalist_with_serb_alliance reflecting the Federation-channel rupture under the Graz-axis posture) - no vocabulary additions; no new carrier flags. This packet extends the HRHB chain (H1) by one downstream event (was 11, now 12 in `enables_events_runtime`).
staff_assessment: Pragmatic-maximum is the documented historical posture: cantons-plus framing kept HZ HB inside the Vance-Owen ten-province + Owen-Stoltenberg three-republics + Washington Federation + Contact Group 51:49 + Dayton institutional architecture, and the Dayton-confirmed Federation footprint is smaller than peak-1993 HZ HB territorial control. The pragmatic-maximum posture preserves Zagreb's patron channel, sustains the central-Bosnia airbridge logic, and keeps the Geneva / Owen-Stoltenberg / Washington diplomatic circuits open. The minimum_consolidation counterfactual collapses the central-Bosnia pockets diplomatically - abandoning Žepče and the Vitez triangle in exchange for Mostar-plus-western-Herzegovina consolidation paradoxically opens the Federation-track early (alliance_change positive) but ruptures the Croat-nationalist faction inside HZ HB and triggers a Zagreb patron-confidence collapse (Tudjman did not authorize pocket-abandonment in 1993). The expansive_conquest counterfactual carries severe diplomatic-exposure costs: open-conquest framing triggers UN/EU recoil under the UNSCR triple-sanctions framework the Croatia side was signaled through 1993, narrows every diplomatic track, and ruptures the Tudjman scope-restraint channel - Tudjman explicitly cautioned Boban against open-conquest framing per the Tudjman-Šušak scope-restraint memoranda admitted at Prlić Vol. 3. The maximalist_with_serb_alliance counterfactual is the maximum-cost option set: open formalization of the Boban-Karadžić Graz axis triggers UNSCR triple-sanctions equivalent international recoil, ruptures Zagreb's patron-confidence ceiling, closes the Geneva / Owen-Stoltenberg / Contact-Group / Washington diplomatic tracks under the Graz-axis exposure framing, and forecloses the Federation alliance entirely.
trigger_evidence: Summer 1993 HZ HB controls peak territorial footprint (Mostar west bank consolidated 9 May 1993; Central Bosnia Vitez/Busovača/Kiseljak triangle + Žepče exclave; Herzegovina core).
Mate Boban under sustained Tudjman scope-restraint pressure via the Šušak channel through spring-summer 1993 (Prlić Vol. 3 Tudjman Presidential Transcripts).
The Geneva, Owen-Stoltenberg, Contact Group, Washington, and Dayton diplomatic tracks all read the HZ HB scope posture as the operative claim line for territorial allocation.

response_options.label: Pragmatic maximum: cantons-plus Banovina framing
response_options.description: Hold the cantons-plus posture: HZ HB is one of three constitutive ethnic provinces / republics with central-Bosnia and western Herzegovina territorial allocation along the 1939 Banovina template the Vance-Owen and Owen-Stoltenberg plans ratify. The Tudjman-Šušak scope-restraint channel is honored; the central-Bosnia airbridge sustains Žepče and the Vitez triangle through to the Washington framework; the Geneva / Owen-Stoltenberg / Contact Group / Washington diplomatic circuits remain open; the Federation channel is reachable when sanctions pressure on Croatia tightens at March 1994.

response_options.label: Minimum consolidation: pull back to Mostar + western Herzegovina
response_options.description: Concede the central-Bosnia pockets diplomatically: abandon the Vitez triangle and the Žepče exclave as untenable, consolidate to Mostar plus western Herzegovina (Posušje, Grude, Ljubuški, Čitluk, Široki Brijeg, Tomislavgrad). The airbridge is wound down. The Federation-track with Sarajevo opens early on the back of central-Bosnia abandonment (alliance_change positive with RBiH), but the Croat-nationalist faction inside HZ HB revolts against the pocket-abandonment posture, Tudjman's patron-confidence collapses on the unilateral consolidation that defies the spring-1993 airbridge directive, and the territorial-legitimacy claim narrows to the Mostar+Herzegovina footprint that Dayton ultimately confirms.

response_options.label: Expansive conquest: full historical Croat lands claim
response_options.description: Advance the open-conquest framing: full "historical Croat lands" claim including eastern Herzegovina and aggressive central-Bosnia consolidation beyond the Banovina template. The Tudjman-Šušak scope-restraint channel ruptures (Tudjman explicitly cautioned against open-conquest framing per the spring-summer 1993 memoranda admitted at Prlić Vol. 3). UN/EU recoil triggers under the UNSCR triple-sanctions threat the Croatia side was signaled through 1993; international standing collapses; the Geneva / Owen-Stoltenberg / Contact-Group diplomatic tracks narrow severely under the sanctions-pressure framing; the recruitment pool degrades on the back of international isolation; the negotiating-leverage at every downstream track is foreclosed under the open-conquest exposure.

response_options.label: Maximalist claim with formalized Boban-Karadžić Graz axis
response_options.description: Formalize the Boban-Karadžić Graz axis (6 May 1992 joint statement extended into an operative partition arrangement against Sarajevo's central-Bosnia residual). The Tudjman patron-confidence ceiling ruptures (open Belgrade-axis posture defies Zagreb's documented scope-restraint directive). The Federation alliance with RBiH is foreclosed entirely; international-standing collapses under UNSCR triple-sanctions equivalent recoil at the open Boban-Karadžić axis formalization; the Geneva / Owen-Stoltenberg / Contact-Group / Washington diplomatic circuits close under the Graz-axis exposure framing; the negotiating-leverage at every downstream track narrows to the Belgrade-Pale corridor.

RBiH.headline: Mostar holds cantons-plus scope at peak territorial reach
RBiH.body: The HZ HB Presidency keeps the Vance-Owen / Owen-Stoltenberg Banovina-aligned scope as the operative claim line. Sarajevo reads the cantons-plus framing as preserving the Federation-track availability when sanctions pressure on Croatia tightens at the Washington framework.

RS.headline: Mostar declines open-conquest framing
RS.body: The HZ HB Presidency stays inside the cantons-plus Banovina template under Tudjman scope-restraint pressure. Pale reads the diplomatic-track preservation against the partition logic the Graz 1992 joint statement signaled.

RBiH.headline: Mostar concedes central-Bosnia pockets diplomatically
RBiH.body: The HZ HB Presidency abandons the Vitez triangle and Žepče exclave as untenable, consolidating to Mostar plus western Herzegovina. Sarajevo reads the unilateral Federation-track opening against the Croat-nationalist faction revolt that the pocket-abandonment posture triggers inside HZ HB.

RS.headline: Mostar pulls back to Herzegovina core
RS.body: The HZ HB Presidency winds down the central-Bosnia airbridge and consolidates to the Herzegovina footprint. Pale reads the territorial-legitimacy contraction against the Tudjman patron-confidence collapse the unilateral consolidation triggers.

RBiH.headline: Mostar advances open-conquest territorial framing
RBiH.body: The HZ HB Presidency advances the full historical Croat lands claim including eastern Herzegovina. Sarajevo reads the UN/EU recoil and the UNSCR triple-sanctions threat against the Tudjman scope-restraint channel rupture the open-conquest framing triggers.

RS.headline: Mostar pushes maximalist claim line
RS.body: The HZ HB Presidency pushes the open-conquest framing beyond the Banovina template. Pale reads the diplomatic-track narrowing under the sanctions-pressure framing and the Tudjman scope-restraint channel rupture the open-conquest posture triggers.

RBiH.headline: Mostar formalizes Boban-Karadžić Graz axis
RBiH.body: The HZ HB Presidency formalizes the Boban-Karadžić Graz 1992 partition arrangement against Sarajevo's central-Bosnia residual. Sarajevo reads the Federation-track foreclosure and the UNSCR triple-sanctions equivalent international recoil the open Belgrade-axis posture triggers.

RS.headline: Mostar moves to formalize Graz partition axis
RS.body: The HZ HB Presidency formalizes the Boban-Karadžić joint axis against the Sarajevo residual. Pale reads the operational alignment alongside the Tudjman patron-confidence rupture and the UNSCR triple-sanctions equivalent recoil at the open Graz-axis formalization.
