title: Battle of Bugojno
narrative: The ARBiH 307th Brigade attacks HVO positions in Bugojno in central Bosnia, where the defending Eugen Kvaternik Brigade can muster only 200-400 effective troops. After ten days of street fighting the ARBiH secures control of the town and captures significant military equipment, including tanks and artillery, consolidating control over the Vrbas River valley.

effects.text: Bugojno falls and its HVO arsenal is absorbed into the ARBiH. The momentum in central Bosnia has decisively shifted.

historical_source: ICTY Hadzihasanovic Trial Judgment (IT-01-47-T).

title: Sarajevo Market Areas Under Fire
narrative: Repeated mortar and artillery strikes target civilian areas in Sarajevo, including crowded marketplaces. Each incident draws international condemnation and edges the international community closer to considering military intervention against VRS positions. The SRK maintains its bombardment despite cease-fire agreements.
source_note: Existing ICTY/UN and Sarajevo shelling sources ground the row's provenance and institutional context. This note adds no casualty figures, causal claims, prohibited player choices, or alternate-outcome prevention framing.

effects.text: Artillery continues to target civilian areas in Sarajevo. International pressure for intervention builds steadily.

title: Belgrade Grows Distant: Milošević Signals Exhaustion
narrative: After the Owen-Stoltenberg plan collapses, Milošević signals through back-channels that Serbia's patience is exhausted. UN sanctions are cratering the Serbian economy — Pale's demands are no longer Belgrade's priority.

effect.text: Milošević signals through back-channels that Serbia's patience with Pale is exhausted.

title: NATO Threatens Air Strikes — Sarajevo Ultimatum
narrative: NATO formally agrees to launch air strikes against Bosnian Serb positions if the strangulation of Sarajevo or attacks on other safe areas continue. The decision marks the first time the Alliance has authorized potential force in its 44-year history. The dual-key arrangement between UN and NATO commands means execution remains politically constrained, but the threat forces the VRS withdrawal from Mount Igman.

effects.text: NATO's ultimatum is the clearest signal yet that the international community may use force. The VRS calculates its next move carefully.

historical_source: NATO Council decision, August 9 1993. Operation Deny Flight history.

title: Owen-Stoltenberg Plan Proposed
narrative: International mediators David Owen and Thorvald Stoltenberg present a new peace plan proposing a loose union of three ethnic republics. The plan effectively legitimizes ethnic partition and is seen by the Bosnian government as rewarding aggression. Negotiations continue through the autumn amid ongoing fighting on all fronts.

effect.text: The Owen-Stoltenberg Plan proposes a tripartite union of ethnic republics. Each faction must weigh the costs of acceptance or rejection.

response_options.label: Accept the Owen-Stoltenberg Framework
response_options.description: Accepting brings international relief but concedes the principle of a unified Bosnia.

response_options.label: Reject Ethnic Partition
response_options.description: Rejection defends sovereignty but prolongs the war and frustrates mediators.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg
HRHB.body: RBiH accepts the Owen-Stoltenberg framework and gains international relief. HVO leaders see Sarajevo conceding the principle of a unified Bosnia under a tripartite republic formula.

RS.headline: Sarajevo accepts Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: RBiH accepts the proposed union of ethnic republics, improving diplomatic credibility while conceding the unity principle. Pale sees Sarajevo moving onto the mediator track.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo rejects ethnic partition
HRHB.body: RBiH rejects the Owen-Stoltenberg framework as a partition formula. HVO leaders see Sarajevo defending sovereignty while prolonging the war and frustrating mediators.

RS.headline: Sarajevo refuses Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: RBiH rejects the tripartite republic framework and accepts the diplomatic cost. Pale sees Sarajevo preserve its sovereignty claim while mediator pressure rises.

title: Owen-Stoltenberg: Accept or Resist?
narrative: Owen and Stoltenberg present their Union of Three Republics plan aboard HMS Invincible (20 September 1993). The Presidency narrowly accepted, conditional on territorial concessions in eastern Bosnia (the Drina enclaves and Posavina corridor). The decision now falls to the Sarajevo Assembly (29 September 1993): ratify the Presidency's conditional acceptance, or reject the partition formula outright.
historical_source: UN S/26486 (23 September 1993, ICFY transmission of the Invincible package, records RBiH Presidency conditional acceptance of 20 September 1993 at Geneva); UN S/26922 (21 December 1993, ICFY Steering Committee Report documenting the RBiH Assembly rejection of 29 September 1993); ICTY Prosecutor v. Karadžić Trial Judgement IT-95-5/18-T vol. III §§4263-4310 (esp. §§4280-4310 on September 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg outcomes); Bosnian Presidency Sarajevo Assembly session records 29 September 1993; David Owen, Balkan Odyssey (1995); Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II (operational context for Drina enclaves and Posavina corridor situation driving Assembly rejection).
source_note: The row represents the documented two-step Owen-Stoltenberg sequence: Presidency narrow acceptance 20 September 1993 conditional on territorial concessions, followed by Assembly outright rejection 29 September 1993 citing the unrecoverable Drina enclaves and the Posavina corridor cession. The historical default `reject_via_assembly` is the documented joint outcome. The counterfactual `accept_for_optics` reflects an alternative parliamentary current that could have ratified the Presidency's conditional acceptance.
staff_assessment: Assembly rejection preserves the principle of a unified multi-ethnic Bosnia and the legal claim to the Drina enclaves at the cost of immediate international standing and negotiating-leverage erosion. Acceptance for optics could pressure Pale diplomatically but legitimizes the partition framework and carries Presidency/Assembly procedural rupture.
trigger_evidence: The Owen-Stoltenberg plan has reached the Bosnian government (per owen_stoltenberg_plan_1993).
Presidency accepted on 20 September 1993 aboard HMS Invincible conditional on Drina-enclaves and Posavina-corridor concessions (UN S/26486).
The Assembly session of 29 September 1993 is the decisive vote (UN S/26922).

effect.text: The Owen-Stoltenberg plan reaches the Sarajevo Assembly. The Presidency's narrow Invincible acceptance is on the table; the Assembly must ratify or reject the partition framework.

response_options.label: Assembly rejects outright (Drina enclaves & Posavina non-negotiable)
response_options.description: The Sarajevo Assembly votes down the Presidency's conditional acceptance, refusing the Drina-enclaves and Posavina-corridor cession. The plan collapses; the war continues but the legal claim to Bosnia's full territory is preserved.

response_options.label: Assembly ratifies the Presidency's conditional acceptance
response_options.description: An alternative parliamentary majority ratifies what the Presidency initialed aboard HMS Invincible. Sarajevo gains international standing while legitimizing the partition formula and accepting the Drina-enclaves and Posavina-corridor concessions in principle.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo Assembly rejects Owen-Stoltenberg
HRHB.body: The Bosnian Assembly votes down the Union of Three Republics plan, refusing the Drina enclaves and Posavina corridor cession. HVO leaders see Sarajevo preserve its sovereignty claim and negotiating leverage while accepting the cost to international standing.

RS.headline: Sarajevo Assembly rejects Owen-Stoltenberg
RS.body: The Bosnian Assembly votes down the Invincible package outright. Pale sees Sarajevo refuse partition on principle, prolonging the war and frustrating the ICFY mediators.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo Assembly ratifies the Invincible package
HRHB.body: The Bosnian Assembly ratifies the Presidency's conditional acceptance of the Owen-Stoltenberg framework. HVO leaders see Sarajevo gain international standing while legitimizing partition in principle.

RS.headline: Sarajevo Assembly ratifies for diplomatic leverage
RS.body: The Bosnian Assembly ratifies the Owen-Stoltenberg framework while calculating that Pale will reject its territorial allocation. RS staff see Sarajevo trying to isolate them diplomatically.

title: Sarajevo Records Its Arms-Embargo Lift Advocacy Posture
narrative: The Sarajevo Presidency must record its diplomatic posture toward the UNSCR 713 arms embargo applied to all of former-Yugoslavia in September 1991. Throughout 1993, Izetbegović has addressed the UN General Assembly and the US Congress directly arguing the embargo asymmetrically privileges the JNA-armed VRS and HVO over the under-armed ARBiH; Prime Minister Silajdžić has run a shuttle-diplomacy circuit (Washington, London, Bonn, Riyadh) lobbying for embargo lift and NATO air strikes against VRS positions. The US Senate is preparing a lift-and-strike resolution (passed by 70-30 in August 1993; vetoed by Clinton). In parallel, the covert Iran arms channel via Croatia transshipment is operating, alongside Mujahideen-brigade volunteer flow. The Presidency must declare its public posture: lobby openly for lift-and-strike (the documented historical posture across 1993-1995); pursue clandestine arms acquisition through Iran/Croatia (parallel-track operational but politically exposing if surfaced); abandon embargo advocacy as a lost cause and focus on diplomatic settlement under existing constraints; or accept the embargo as binding international law and rule-following discipline.

effect.text: Sarajevo records its arms-embargo lift-and-strike advocacy posture for the UN General Assembly, US Congress, and Contact Group diplomatic circuits.

source_note: UNSCR 713 (25 September 1991) applied a comprehensive arms embargo to all of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. Throughout 1993-1995, the Sarajevo Presidency under Alija Izetbegović and Prime Minister Haris Silajdžić ran a sustained diplomatic offensive lobbying for: (a) lifting the UNSCR 713 embargo on the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina specifically (the asymmetric-application argument: the JNA-armed VRS and Croatia-armed HVO faced an under-armed ARBiH because the embargo froze the pre-war Yugoslav force distribution), and (b) NATO air strikes against VRS positions (lift-and-strike). The US Senate passed lift-and-strike resolutions on 11 August 1993 (S.J. Res. 110, 70-30) and again in July-August 1995 (Bob Dole/Joseph Lieberman amendment, passed 69-29; vetoed by Clinton on 11 August 1995, override failed). Izetbegović addressed the UN General Assembly repeatedly demanding embargo lift; Silajdžić shuttle diplomacy circulated Washington-London-Bonn-Riyadh-Tehran 1993-1995. The covert Iran arms channel via Croatia transshipment (the 'no-instructions' US tacit acquiescence channel of April 1994, the Croatian 25% transit-tax arrangement) operated 1992-1995 in parallel; Mujahideen-brigade volunteer recruitment (the 7th Muslim Brigade / El Mudžahid Detachment in 3rd Corps) drew on the same patron channel. The lift-and-strike advocacy was the defining RBiH external diplomatic posture across 1993-1995. Sources: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II (CIA Office of Russian and European Analysis 2002) — 1993-95 ARBiH supply chronology + Silajdžić diplomatic posture; Alija Izetbegović, 'Inescapable Questions: Autobiographical Notes' (Islamic Foundation 2003) — UN General Assembly addresses + lift-and-strike argumentation; Richard Holbrooke, 'To End A War' (Random House 1998) chs. 4-6 — Clinton administration deliberation on lift-and-strike, August 1995 endgame; US Senate Foreign Relations Committee records (S.J. Res. 110 vote and (in due course) the 1995 Dole-Lieberman amendment. The moral-high-ground appeal in Western public opinion generates negotiating leverage at the Contact Group and Washington tracks; the Bosniak-hawk faction supports the legitimate-grievance external advocacy; US and EU partners face diplomatic pressure to act on the asymmetric-application argument.

response_options.label: Pursue clandestine arms acquisition
response_options.description: Endorse openly the covert Iran arms channel and Croatia transshipment arrangement. The ARBiH supply pool grows on the back of Iran-routed shipments; the 7th Muslim Brigade and El Mudžahid Detachment recruitment is consolidated through the same patron channel. Western diplomatic exposure is acute if surfaced: Clinton administration disavowal triggers a patron-confidence collapse with Washington; EU partners recoil at the public endorsement of UN-embargo circumvention; the negotiating-leverage framework at the Contact Group track narrows. The operational supply boost is meaningful (~5,000 tons of arms over the 1992-1995 window per the documented Croatia transit-tax arrangement) but not transformative given ARBiH's overall personnel pool.

response_options.label: Abandon lift-and-strike advocacy
response_options.description: Concede the UNSCR 713 framework as durable international law and stand down the lift-and-strike diplomatic offensive. The external-pressure framework at the Contact Group and Washington tracks collapses; the moral-high-ground appeal in Western public opinion atrophies; the Bosniak-hawk faction inside the Presidency revolts against the perceived capitulation. The diplomatic horizon narrows to whatever settlement can be reached under the asymmetric force-correlation that the embargo locks in.

response_options.label: Accept the embargo as binding international law
response_options.description: Make rule-following discipline an explicit Presidency posture: the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina accepts UNSCR 713 as binding international law and forecloses both the lift-and-strike argument and the covert Iran channel. The international-standing return is modest (a rule-following reward in Western legal-discipline frames) but the negotiating-leverage cost is severe: the external-pressure framework collapses entirely, the military-credibility hit from de facto acceptance of force-correlation weakness compounds, and the Bosniak-hawk faction reads the posture as legitimizing the asymmetric-application embargo against Sarajevo itself. The hard-line revolt against the Presidency line is the maximum internal-cohesion cost in the option set.

title: Owen-Stoltenberg: Mostar Records Its Posture
narrative: Owen and Stoltenberg's Union of Three Republics plan was tabled aboard HMS Invincible on 20 September 1993. The map ratifies Herceg-Bosna as one of three constitutive ethnic republics, with the central-Bosnia and western Herzegovina territorial allocation drawn favorably to Croat claims. Zagreb's directive is unambiguous: Tudjman has signaled to Boban that the HZ HB Presidency is to sign. The Mostar Presidency must record its posture toward the Invincible package — accept the Union of Three Republics framework, reject the plan and break with Zagreb's directive, or condition acceptance on territorial amendments in central Bosnia.

title: The Cameras Turn to Heliodrom
narrative: International journalists and ICRC delegates have reached the HVO detention facilities in Herzegovina. The Heliodrom complex near Mostar, the Dretelj barracks, the Gabela warehouse — images of Bosniak men, including former HVO soldiers, held in overcrowded conditions reach the international press. Belgrade's camps were the defining humanitarian crisis of 1992; Heliodrom and Dretelj are becoming the defining humanitarian crisis of 1993. Zagreb's patron channel is alarmed; Tudjman's office is fielding direct calls from Washington and Bonn. The HZ HB Presidency must record its posture toward the international exposure.

title: Belgrade Calls: Pale Records Its Posture
narrative: Milosevic's envoys arrive at Pale through the FRY-RS channel. The directive is unambiguous: ease the Drina-corridor tempo, signal flexibility on Sarajevo division, and accept the corridor-narrowing implied by the Owen-Stoltenberg track and the diplomatic envelope Belgrade is brokering. The pressure is diplomatic, not material — no embargo, no border closure, no supply rupture. But Belgrade is exhausted by sanctions and the patron channel matters for ammunition reliability and political cover at the Security Council. Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic disagree on the response. The Pale Assembly must record its posture: defy the directive on principle, accept the directive and adjust operations, partially comply by signaling some flexibility without breaking the platform, or attempt to broker a compromise that preserves Pale's leverage.

effect.text: Pale records its posture toward Belgrade's soft diplomatic pressure on the Owen-Stoltenberg / pre-embargo channel.

source_note: Belgrade-Pale soft diplomatic pressure was an intermittent thread across the war's mid-period (1993-1995). Milosevic applied diplomatic — not material — pressure on the Pale leadership (Karadzic, Krajisnik, Mladic) to accept successive peace plans (VOPP, Owen-Stoltenberg, Contact Group); Pale repeatedly defied these overtures short of the formal August 1994 FRY embargo. The autumn 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg-adjacent window is the densest documented soft-pressure phase: Belgrade brokered the Invincible package signature track but Pale's tempo on the Drina-corridor and Sarajevo-axis operations diverged from the diplomatic envelope, producing the patron-channel friction Karadzic IT-95-5/18-T Vol. III §§4263-4310 documents on the Pale side. Sources: ICTY Krajisnik IT-00-39-T Trial Judgment (27 September 2006) §§1006-1040 (Pale leadership response to Belgrade pressure on diplomatic envelope, 1993-1994); ICTY Karadzic IT-95-5/18-T Trial Judgment (24 March 2016) Vol. III §§4263-4310 (FRY-RS channel friction across the autumn 1993 - August 1994 corridor); ICTY Milosevic IT-02-54-T (FRY-RS channel context; Belgrade's diplomatic envelope and patron-pressure modulation); Richard Holbrooke, To End a War (Random House 1998) chs. 4-5 (Belgrade-Pale split as defining political-military thread of the war's mid-period; soft diplomatic pressure phase distinct from the August 1994 embargo); David Owen, Balkan Odyssey (Harcourt 1995) ch. 7 (Belgrade-brokered Invincible package; Pale acquiescence pattern); Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II Ch. 11 (FRY-RS channel modulation through the autumn 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg window and across the 1993-1994 Contact Group prelude). This row is DISTINCT from R8 (`belgrade_embargo_rs_1994`, war_1994.json turn 121-122): R7 covers the SOFT diplomatic-pressure phase (1993 — no material embargo, no border closure, no supply rupture); R8 covers the HARD material embargo response (4 August 1994 onward — FRY border closure, supply rupture, UNSCR 943 of 23 September 1994 endorsement). Cost-floor topology reflects the soft/hard distinction: R7 lever pulls patron-confidence + international-standing + internal-cohesion via political signalling; R8 lever pulls supply_delta, patron_pressure, recruitment_modifier via material rupture. §3.6 forward-looking guard: any future `csq_rs_belgrade_pressure_*` row consuming this row's outcomes MUST NOT re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, hostage-taking, civilian-targeting, paramilitary deployment, or any sensitive-act response option. This is a CONSTITUTIONAL-POLITICAL crisis lane (Belgrade-Pale patron-channel friction; Karadzic-Milosevic split politics) — NOT operational ethnic-targeting. The Drina-corridor cleansing, Sarajevo-siege fires, Srebrenica enclave operations, and any associated atrocity surfaces remain canon-gated through their existing event surfaces (rs_drina_campaign, rs_camp_exposure_response, un_safe_area_enforcement, un_hostage_crisis_1995 family slugs). Engine vocabulary substitutions per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md: counterfactual accept costs Pale hawks (internal_cohesion -20) + boosts patron_confidence (+20) and international_standing (+10); historical defy keeps internal cohesion intact and burns negotiating leverage; partial compliance and broker-compromise occupy the middle band with proportional shifts. New event reuses existing RS_BRANCH_TAGS entries (`rs_belgrade_pale_resist`, `rs_belgrade_pale_acknowledge`, `rs_belgrade_negotiate`) — no vocabulary additions; no new carrier flags.
staff_assessment: Defying Belgrade's directive is the documented Pale posture across the soft-pressure 1993-1995 window: Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic agreed the platform mattered more than the patron channel until the August 1994 embargo forced re-evaluation. Acceptance is the maximum-cost counterfactual — Belgrade is satisfied (patron_confidence +20) and the West signals approval (international_standing +10), but Pale hawks rebel and internal cohesion collapses by 20, with a six-turn recruitment penalty (0.90x pool). Partial compliance and brokered compromise occupy the middle band: smaller patron gains, proportional internal-cohesion costs. The Russian channel and the Patriarchate moderate the cost floor on broker-compromise (negotiating_leverage +10 captures the Holbrooke-era diplomatic optionality).

response_options.description: Reject the FRY envoys' demand. response_options.label: Accept Belgrade's directive
response_options.description: Honor Milosevic's request. Ease the Drina-corridor tempo, signal flexibility on Sarajevo, and align the Pale posture with the FRY diplomatic envelope. Belgrade is satisfied; international standing rises. But Pale hawks rebel: Mladic and the Assembly hardliners challenge the leadership, internal cohesion collapses, and recruitment suffers for six turns as the platform faction questions the political track.

response_options.description: Signal some flexibility to Belgrade without breaking the platform. response_options.description: Open back-channels through Patriarch Pavle and the Russian envoys. Offer Belgrade a face-saving formula that preserves the Six Strategic Goals platform while signalling diplomatic engagement on the Owen-Stoltenberg envelope. The patron channel strengthens and negotiating leverage rises; internal cohesion takes a small hit from the optical compromise.

title: Abdic Declares the Autonomous Province
narrative: Sarajevo Presidency files, 27 September 1993. Fikret Abdic — the Velika Kladusa industrialist who polled ahead of Izetbegovic on the joint Presidency list in November 1990, and who has rejected the Presidency's positions on the Owen-Stoltenberg framework — has today declared the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia centered on Velika Kladusa. Una-Sana economic ties with the Republic of Serbian Krajina and Pale-aligned channels are documented. The 5th Corps in Bihac now faces a second internal front to the north as well as the external siege from the south and west. The Presidency must record a posture toward the breakaway entity: suppress it militarily through 5th Corps clearance operations, tolerate it for now and concentrate on the external siege, offer Federation-line negotiating channels, or open formal talks on a negotiated autonomy that recognizes Abdic's seat at the table.

effect.text: The Sarajevo Presidency records a posture toward the Abdic / APWB declaration of 27 September 1993.

effects.text: The Sarajevo Presidency awaits the political record on the Bihac-pocket internal front opened by the Abdic declaration.

Any future `csq_rbih_apwb_*` row consuming `rbih_abdic_relationship` outcomes MUST NOT re-author atrocity, cleansing, forced-displacement, hostage-taking, or any other sensitive-act response option; APWB suppression is well-attested Bihac-pocket warfare but downstream consequence rows must stay within legitimate military lanes. The worksheet's `national_identity` cost-floor framing is encoded engine-side as `internal_cohesion` shifts (the canonical proxy in `strategic_dimensions.ts`, since `national_identity` is not a registered DimensionId). Cost floors per task spec + Game Designer Wave 1 review on packet v1.1 precedent (B-A batch) prevent counterfactual dominance of the historical `suppress_apwb` line. Fikret Abdic verdict 31 July 2002.
staff_assessment: Suppressing the breakaway mirrors the documented Sarajevo posture of non-recognition and 5th Corps clearance operations; Velika Kladusa is briefly cleared in August 1994 and the post-Storm clearance in August 1995 closes the lane. Tolerating the split preserves immediate 5th Corps capacity for the external siege but lets the APWB internal front fester, paying recruitment and cohesion costs as the SDA hardline current reads the decision as Sarajevo accepting fragmentation. Offering Federation-line channels signals openness to a U.S.-backed dual-track solution but Belgrade-aligned Abdic reads it as Sarajevo weakness; patron pressure rises and negotiating leverage drops. Opening formal autonomy talks functionally legitimizes the APWB and pays heavy cohesion / recruitment costs as 5th Corps cadres read the decision as Sarajevo betrayal at the moment of crisis.

Costs are paid in 5th Corps personnel and Bihac-pocket supply; the political-recruit posture stays intact.

title: Bosnian Parliament Rejects Owen-Stoltenberg Plan
narrative: After sessions aboard HMS Invincible on September 20, the Bosnian government assembly in Sarajevo votes to reject the Owen-Stoltenberg plan's ethnic partition, demanding additional territory and access to the sea. The rejection prolongs the war and frustrates international mediators but preserves the principle of a unified, multi-ethnic Bosnia.

effects.text: The Bosnian assembly refuses partition. The war will continue — but so will Bosnia's legal claim to its full territory.

historical_source: Peace plans proposed before and during the Bosnian War. HMS Invincible negotiations, September 20 1993.

title: Abdic-Karadzic Pact
narrative: Fikret Abdic signs a declaration with RS President Radovan Karadzic recognizing the Autonomous Province of Western Bosnia's sovereignty. The VRS commits to non-aggression, joint defense coordination, and logistical support including arms supplies, while the RSK also provides backing. The pact transforms the Bihac pocket into a three-way battleground: 5th Corps against Abdic's APWB forces backed by both Serb entities.

effects.text: Abdic and Karadzic formalize their alliance. The 5th Corps now faces encirclement from three directions — VRS, RSK, and APWB.

historical_source: Abdic-Karadzic Declaration, Oct 22 1993. ICTY Karadzic Trial Judgment (IT-95-5/18-T).

title: Stupni Do Massacre
narrative: HVO special units 'Apostoli' and 'Maturice' under Ivica Rajic attack the Bosniak village of Stupni Do near Vares, killing approximately 31 civilians and destroying the village. Over 250 Bosniak men in nearby Vares are rounded up and subjected to inhuman treatment. When UNPROFOR attempts to investigate, HVO forces obstruct access for days before the evidence is documented.

effects.text: Stupni Do is added to the growing list of documented HVO atrocities. Rajic will eventually plead guilty at The Hague.

historical_source: ICTY Rajic Sentencing Judgment (IT-95-12-S).

title: Reintegration Offers to Serb and Croat Communities
narrative: The Sarajevo Presidency closes the autumn 1993 policy window. The May Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen and the 29 September Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg have foreclosed both internationally-brokered partition frameworks. Roughly 70% of pre-war Bosnia sits outside Sarajevo's effective control: Krajina, Posavina, eastern Herzegovina, and the Drina valley under VRS; western Herzegovina and central-Bosnia pockets under HVO. The Presidency must record an explicit policy posture toward the populations in those territories. Does Sarajevo maintain its maximalist civic-state claim and rely on military pressure as the principal reintegration vehicle, or does it open explicit autonomy / federation offers to Serb-majority and Croat-majority communities under enemy faction control? The pre-Washington HRHB federation channel is operative on the Croat side; no comparable framework has been tabled toward the RS-held communities. Internal SDA debate has surfaced both wider-autonomy proposals and rejection of any symmetric framework with RS.

effect.text: The Sarajevo Presidency records its posture toward reintegration paths offered to Serb-majority and Croat-majority communities outside its effective control.

source_note: Following the May 1993 RS Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen and the 29 September 1993 RBiH Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg, the Sarajevo Presidency had to crystallize its policy posture toward the populations of territories under VRS and HVO control. The documented historical posture was maintain_offensive_posture: the Presidency consistently maintained a maximalist territorial claim framed through the civic-republic platform (one Bosnia, equal citizenship) and relied primarily on military pressure plus diplomatic legitimacy advocacy as the principal vehicles for reintegration, rather than offering explicit autonomy frameworks to RS-held communities. The principal exception was the pre-Washington HRHB federation channel: U.S.-brokered Croat-Bosniak rapprochement was operative through autumn 1993 and crystallized in the Washington Agreement of 1 + 18 March 1994 (rbih_washington_agreement_1994 + hrhb_washington_agreement_1994). No comparable framework was tabled toward the RS-held communities; the documented SDA-Assembly debates record proposals for wider-autonomy frameworks but they were rejected on the Bosniak-hawks faction reading that symmetric concession to RS would ratify the partition logic the May/September Assembly rejections had foreclosed. The offer_federation_status counterfactual extends the documented HRHB federation channel symmetrically toward RS as an explicit diplomatic offer (international_standing + negotiating_leverage gain, but Bosniak-hawks revolt cost on internal_cohesion); the conditional_autonomy_proposal counterfactual offers reintegration on terms (acceptance of RBiH sovereignty) consistent with the civic-state claim but unprecedented in scope (modest international_standing + negotiating_leverage gain, modest internal_cohesion cost from hawks faction); the accept_de_facto_partition counterfactual concedes the maximalist civic-state claim and is the maximum-cost variant (territorial_legitimacy -40 + military_credibility -25 + internal_cohesion -25 + international_standing -10 + alliance_change -0.05). Sources: Balkan Battlegrounds Vol. II — 1993-94 RBiH diplomatic posture chronology; Alija Izetbegović, Inescapable Questions (Islamic Foundation 2003) on the autumn-1993 maximalist-claim policy crystallization and Washington Agreement framework; Haris Silajdžić foreign policy correspondence + UN General Assembly addresses 1993-94 on the maximalist civic-state external-advocacy framework; Washington Agreement text 1 + 18 March 1994 + Vienna Framework 26 March 1994 (HRHB federation channel anchor); ICTY Karadžić IT-95-5/18-T §§4263-4310 on the September 1993 Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg and the maximalist-claim institutional posture; ICTY Halilović IT-01-48-T on ARBiH General Staff doctrine 1993-94 (military pressure as primary reintegration vehicle); UN S/26486 + UN S/26922 (UNSG reports on the autumn-1993 diplomatic framework). Engine vocabulary substitutions per memory/engine_dimension_vocabulary.md: alliance_lock(hrhb) collapsed to alliance_change (Federation alliance proxy); territorial_loss collapsed to territorial_legitimacy (proxy for the maximalist civic-state claim). §3.6 STRICT forward-looking guard (Wave 2 Canon): any future csq_rbih_reintegration_* event authored to consume rbih_reintegration_offers_1993 outcomes MUST NOT carry response options that re-author cleansing, forced-displacement, civilian-targeting, hostage-taking, paramilitary-deployment, ethnic-targeting, or any sensitive-act response option. This packet's DECISION is constitutional/diplomatic (territorial-claim posture + reintegration-framework posture toward populations under enemy faction control), NOT operational-ethnic. The sensitive humanitarian surfaces of the war (drina_cleansing_decision_1992, concentration_camps_revealed_1992, ahmici_massacre_1993, stupni_do_massacre_1993, mostar_bridge_destroyed_1993, grabovica_uzdol_massacres_1993, srebrenica_demilitarization_1993, un_hostage_crisis_1995) remain canon-gated through their existing event surfaces; no csq_rbih_reintegration_* descendant may re-open or re-author them. Each counterfactual carries its cost floors on diplomatic / cohesion / legitimacy dimensions; no counterfactual rewards displacement, cleansing, civilian-column attack, or paramilitary deployment.
staff_assessment: Maintaining the offensive posture preserves the maximalist civic-state claim that the May/September 1993 Assembly rejections of Vance-Owen and Owen-Stoltenberg structurally rest on, sustains internal cohesion against Bosniak-hawks revolt, and keeps the Federation channel intact for the pre-Washington HRHB track. Explicit federation offers to RS communities buy international standing and negotiating leverage at the price of internal cohesion (Bosniak hawks read symmetric concession as ratifying partition). The conditional autonomy proposal threads the needle (RBiH sovereignty preserved as the precondition), but is unprecedented in scope. Accepting de facto partition collapses the maximalist civic-state claim at the constitutional level and ruptures both internal cohesion and Federation alliance momentum.
trigger_evidence: The RS Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen (May 1993) and the RBiH Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg (29 September 1993) have foreclosed both internationally-brokered partition frameworks.

response_options.label: Maintain offensive posture -- military pressure as the principal reintegration vehicle
response_options.description: Sarajevo records the maximalist civic-state claim as the operative policy: one Bosnia, equal citizenship, all pre-war territory legitimately RBiH. Reintegration of RS-held and HVO-held populations proceeds principally through military pressure plus diplomatic legitimacy advocacy; no explicit autonomy or federation framework is tabled toward RS-held communities. The pre-Washington HRHB federation channel remains operative on the Croat side via U.S. shuttle diplomacy, but no comparable framework is offered toward RS. The Presidency preserves its constitutional claim against any partition logic the May/September Assembly rejections foreclosed.

response_options.label: Offer federation status to Serb and Croat communities
response_options.description: The Presidency extends the pre-Washington HRHB federation channel symmetrically: explicit federation-status offers are tabled toward both Serb-majority and Croat-majority communities outside RBiH effective control. Each community would retain substantial local autonomy under a federal RBiH constitutional shell. The international community reads the symmetric framework as a major diplomatic concession that preserves the civic-state architecture while accommodating ethnic-territorial reality. Bosniak hawks within SDA and the Sarajevo Assembly read symmetric concession to RS as ratifying the partition logic the May/September Assembly rejections foreclosed; internal cohesion fractures sharply. The HRHB delegation reads the offer as the pre-Washington framework's natural extension and alliance momentum strengthens.

response_options.label: Conditional autonomy proposal -- offer autonomy on RBiH sovereignty acceptance
response_options.description: Sarajevo tables a conditional framework: Serb-majority and Croat-majority communities outside RBiH effective control may receive substantial local autonomy on the precondition that they accept RBiH sovereignty under the unitary civic-state constitution. The framework threads the needle between the maximalist civic-state claim (sovereignty preserved as the precondition) and explicit reintegration outreach (autonomy framework offered on terms). The international community reads the proposal as a constructive Sarajevo move that preserves the May/September Assembly rejections while opening a structured reintegration channel. Bosniak hawks read the conditional offer as more palatable than symmetric federation status because RBiH sovereignty stays the precondition, though some hawks resist any offer to RS. The HRHB delegation reads the conditional framework as compatible with the pre-Washington channel's underlying logic.

response_options.label: Accept de facto partition -- concede the maximalist civic-state claim
response_options.description: The Presidency signals acceptance of the existing front lines as the de facto partition basis: RS retains the Krajina + Posavina + eastern Herzegovina + Drina valley; HVO retains western Herzegovina + central-Bosnia pockets; RBiH consolidates within the existing perimeter. The maximalist civic-state claim is conceded at the constitutional level; the May/September Assembly rejections are structurally unwound. Internal cohesion fractures as the Assembly nationalist current reads the concession as foundational betrayal. International standing collapses on the perception that Sarajevo has conceded de facto partition before any framework is agreed at the negotiating table; the Federation alliance momentum frays as HRHB reads the choice as a Bosniak concession that forecloses Croat territorial reintegration claims. Military credibility collapses on the perception that the ARBiH offensive doctrine has been declared obsolete by Sarajevo itself.

RS.headline: Sarajevo maintains maximalist territorial claim
RS.body: The Sarajevo Presidency records its operative policy: one Bosnia, equal citizenship, all pre-war territory legitimately RBiH. Reintegration proceeds principally through military pressure plus diplomatic legitimacy advocacy. No federation or autonomy offer is tabled toward RS-held communities. Pale reads the posture as institutional continuity with the May Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen and the September Assembly rejection of Owen-Stoltenberg.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo holds maximalist claim with HRHB channel open
HRHB.body: The Sarajevo Presidency records the maximalist civic-state claim as operative policy but keeps the pre-Washington HRHB federation channel open via U.S. shuttle diplomacy. Mostar reads the posture as compatible with the Croat-Bosniak rapprochement track Tudjman and Boban are working through.

RS.headline: Sarajevo tables federation offer to Serb communities
RS.body: The Sarajevo Presidency extends the pre-Washington HRHB federation channel symmetrically toward RS-held communities. Pale assesses the offer as a major diplomatic concession that preserves the civic-state architecture while accommodating ethnic-territorial reality.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo extends Federation framework
HRHB.body: The Sarajevo Presidency offers federation status symmetrically to Serb-majority and Croat-majority communities. Mostar reads the offer as the pre-Washington framework's natural extension; the Croat-Bosniak alliance strengthens.

RS.headline: Sarajevo offers conditional autonomy on sovereignty acceptance
RS.body: The Sarajevo Presidency tables substantial local autonomy for Serb-majority communities on the precondition of RBiH sovereignty acceptance under the unitary civic-state constitution. Pale assesses the framework as a constructive Sarajevo move that preserves the May Assembly rejection of Vance-Owen while opening a structured reintegration channel.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo opens conditional reintegration framework
HRHB.body: The Sarajevo Presidency offers substantial local autonomy on RBiH sovereignty acceptance. Mostar reads the conditional framework as compatible with the pre-Washington channel's underlying logic and Federation alliance momentum strengthens.

RS.headline: Sarajevo signals partition acceptance on existing lines
RS.body: The Sarajevo Presidency signals acceptance of the existing front lines as the de facto partition basis. Pale assesses a maximum diplomatic windfall: the maximalist civic-state claim is conceded at the constitutional level and the May/September Assembly rejections are structurally unwound.

HRHB.headline: Sarajevo concedes maximalist claim
HRHB.body: The Sarajevo Presidency signals acceptance of the existing front lines. Mostar reads the choice as a Bosniak concession that forecloses Croat territorial reintegration claims and Federation alliance momentum frays.

title: Stari Most Destroyed in Mostar
narrative: HVO forces destroy the iconic Stari Most, the 16th-century Ottoman bridge spanning the Neretva River in Mostar. The deliberate demolition of this UNESCO-recognized cultural monument becomes a global symbol of the war's cultural devastation. The act draws widespread international condemnation and deepens the stigma on the Bosnian Croat war effort.

effects.text: The Stari Most is destroyed by HVO shelling. The loss of the iconic bridge becomes a symbol of cultural destruction.

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: The war enters another grinding phase. Your army holds — barely. The international community offers sympathy but not intervention. Your commanders request more men, more guns, more time. The corridors are strained, the enclaves are fragile, and the political situation in Sarajevo grows more tense with each week of siege. What is your posture for the months ahead?

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: The international community grows increasingly hostile. Belgrade's patience with Pale is wearing thin. Your generals report that the lines are solid — but the sanctions bite deeper each month, and the VRS cannot sustain current operational tempo indefinitely. The question before you is not whether you can win, but what victory means in a war the world wants to end.

response_options.description: Engage the international mediators from a position of military advantage. Belgrade's pressure becomes manageable if you demonstrate willingness to talk — while holding every kilometer.

response_options.label: Accept a partition framework
response_options.description: The war has cost more than our people can bear. Signal willingness to accept a territorial settlement in exchange for international recognition. The hardliners in the Assembly will revolt — but the alternative is permanent isolation.

title: Strategic Posture Review
narrative: Zagreb's expectations grow heavier with each passing month. The HVO holds territory across Herzegovina, but central Bosnia slips away and the war with the Bosniaks bleeds both sides white. Tudjman watches the map. Your assembly watches Tudjman. What direction will Herceg-Bosna take in the months ahead?

title: Federation Backchannel: Boban Tests The Language
narrative: In late autumn 1993, the diplomatic ground beneath Herceg-Bosna shifts. Tudjman, recalculating after the failed Owen-Stoltenberg Union of Three Republics framework, the territorial setbacks in central Bosnia following the ARBiH September-October counter-offensive, and the tightening US sanctions pressure on Croatia, signals to Boban that a federation overture to Sarajevo would buy diplomatic room. The channel is back: through Peter Galbraith (the new US Ambassador to Zagreb, accredited 28 June 1993), through Hannes Swoboda's German Christian Democratic foreign-policy office, through the Holbrooke Bonn-Geneva shuttle. Boban convenes the HZ HB Presidency. The Washington Agreement is still months away. The decision is whether to extend the federation overture NOW (October-December 1993) — pre-empting US pressure, capturing diplomatic credit, and creating the negotiating space that will eventually produce the formal Washington signature in March 1994. Or maintain the separate-state line and let Zagreb-hawks dictate the pace. Or condition federation acceptance on canton-level Croat institutional protections. Or reject the federation path entirely and commit to a permanent separate Croat republic. The choice DOES NOT replace H4 (Zagreb-ordered ceasefire, February 1994) or H9 (Washington Agreement, March 1994) — it captures the BACKCHANNEL window BEFORE both, where the diplomatic ground was being prepared.

effect.text: Herceg-Bosna decides whether to extend a federation backchannel overture to Sarajevo before the Washington Agreement framework formalizes.

Tudjman's strategic recalculation followed the Owen-Stoltenberg failure, the Croatian Krajina front pressure (Maslenica/Medak Pocket frictions), the visible US sanctions trajectory on Croatia (US Treasury Croatia-FRY material-pressure preparation), and the accumulating ARBiH territorial pressure in central Bosnia (September-October 1993 ARBiH counter-offensive against HVO pockets). title: Independence Or Autonomy: Pale Crystallizes Its Path
narrative: Between the May 1993 Pale Assembly's rejection of Vance-Owen at Bijeljina and the looming Contact Group framework, the RS leadership crystallizes its general posture decision. Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic confer at Pale. Belgrade's intermittent signalling — through the Owen-Stoltenberg envelope, through Patriarch Pavle, through Milosevic's private envoys — has made clear that a negotiated-autonomy framework within Bosnia and Herzegovina (Knin-style autonomous province, asymmetric federation entity status, or minority-rights-only constitutional package) is the path of least international resistance and could end the FRY sanctions regime that is exhausting the patron state. The platform faction (Pale hawks, Assembly hardliners, the VRS Main Staff) reads any autonomy framework as a betrayal of the Six Strategic Goals. The decision is not specific to any one peace plan — it is the GENERAL posture between specific plan-response windows. Pursue full independent state status. Negotiate autonomy within BiH. Accept Federation entity status. Or accept minority rights only.

effect.text: Pale crystallizes its general posture decision between independence trajectory and negotiated-autonomy fallback frameworks.

source_note: Between the May 1993 Pale Assembly's rejection of Vance-Owen at Bijeljina (5-6 May 1993) and the August 1994 Pale Assembly's rejection of the Contact Group 51/49 framework, RS leadership had repeated decision moments about whether to pursue full independent state status or accept a negotiated-autonomy fallback framework within BiH (Knin-style autonomous province, asymmetric federation entity status, or minority-rights-only constitutional package). Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic consistently chose the independence path, even when Belgrade signalled willingness to accept negotiated autonomy as the path of least international resistance and the route to ending the FRY sanctions regime. staff_assessment: Pursuing independence is the documented Pale posture across the entire 1993-1995 mid-period: Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic agreed the platform mattered more than the patron channel or the international framework. The maximum-cost counterfactual is accept_minority_rights_only, which concedes the entire Six Strategic Goals platform — patron_pressure spikes (+30) and international_standing rises sharply (+30), but internal_cohesion collapses (-40), military_credibility damages (-20), territorial_legitimacy concedes the maximalist claim (-30), and the entire Pale leadership faces revolt. negotiate_autonomy_within_bih is the moderate counterfactual: Knin-style autonomous province within BiH preserves some of the territorial claim at the cost of independent statehood; Pale hawks revolt (internal_cohesion -15) but the patron channel and negotiating leverage hold. accept_federation_status is the asymmetric-entity counterfactual most aligned with what the Dayton framework eventually produced, but accepting it in 1993-94 would have produced massive Pale-hawk revolt (internal_cohesion -30) and military_credibility damage (-10) even as patron_pressure and international_standing rose. The Russian channel and the Patriarchate moderate the cost floor on negotiate_autonomy_within_bih (negotiating_leverage +15 captures the Holbrooke-era diplomatic optionality).

response_options.label: Pursue full independent state status
response_options.description: Reject any negotiated-autonomy framework. Republika Srpska is a state, not an autonomous province within Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Six Strategic Goals remain the platform; the patron channel will hold the friction; the international community will adjust to reality on the ground. Karadzic, Krajisnik, and Mladic align on independence. The platform faction is reinforced; the territorial claim is defended; the negotiating posture rejects the fallback envelope.

response_options.label: Negotiate autonomy within BiH
response_options.description: Accept the Belgrade-favoured fallback envelope. Republika Srpska becomes a Knin-style autonomous province within Bosnia and Herzegovina, preserving most of the territorial claim but conceding independent statehood. Belgrade is satisfied; the international community signals approval; negotiating leverage rises. But Pale hawks revolt: Mladic and the Assembly hardliners read the autonomy concession as platform betrayal, internal cohesion takes a 15-point hit, and the maximalist territorial-legitimacy claim concedes.

response_options.label: Accept Federation entity status
response_options.description: Accept asymmetric Federation entity status within Bosnia and Herzegovina, anticipating what the Dayton framework will eventually produce. The constitutional architecture is bipolar but Republika Srpska survives as a constitutional entity with broad self-governance. Belgrade is satisfied; the international community signals strong approval; the bilateral alliance proxy with the Federation lifts. But the Pale-hawk revolt is massive: the entire Assembly hardline reads Federation entity status as the betrayal of independence Karadzic has spent the war denouncing, internal cohesion takes a 30-point hit, and military_credibility suffers as the platform's defenders read the move as capitulation.

response_options.label: Accept minority rights only
response_options.description: Concede the entire Six Strategic Goals platform. Republika Srpska dissolves as a territorial-political entity; Bosnian Serbs accept minority-rights protection within a unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina. Belgrade is satisfied; the international community signals strongest approval; sanctions are lifted. But the entire Pale leadership faces crisis: Karadzic's political program collapses, Mladic and the VRS Main Staff repudiate the political track, the Assembly hardliners read the move as total surrender, internal cohesion collapses by 40 points, military_credibility damages by 20, territorial_legitimacy concedes by 30, and the platform faction faction repudiates the leadership outright. This is the maximum-cost counterfactual.
